notes.title: Progression preparation: What to unlock in Black Ops 6, part 1
notes.notes:
[h2]Black Ops 6 Progression: Overview & Goals[/h2]
[i]Call of Duty®: Black Ops 6 [/i]marks the anticipated return of Classic Prestige, back in Call of Duty and bigger than ever…but that’s not the only Progression system that’s gotten a major upgrade this year. The Treyarch team has set out to build the most rewarding Progression and Challenge systems ever delivered in a Call of Duty game, meaning [i]Black Ops 6[/i] packs a ton of unlockable content into the game on Day 1! This blog details everything you’ll need to know about Progression and Unlocks in [i]Black Ops 6[/i] including: Prestige, Calling Card Challenges, Camos, Reticles, the all-new Mastery Badge System, and Medals.

There’s always something to grind for and unlock in [i]Black Ops 6[/i]:
[h3]Systems Covered in this Blog[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/4e7f03d3493972226304964ffbd3aa0d520888cc.jpg[/img]

Here’s a summary of the Progression, Challenge, and Customization systems covered in this blog:

[b]Level Unlocks: [/b]Earn XP in Multiplayer and Zombies (and in Season 01: [i]Call of Duty: Warzone™[/i]) to progress through 55 Levels of unlockable Weapons, Equipment, Scorestreaks, and more.

[b]Prestige: [/b]Classic Prestige is BACK in [i]Black Ops 6[/i] and bigger than ever! Players who reach and complete Max Level 55 will be presented with the choice to enter Prestige and restart their Leveling journey in exchange for a bit of Prestige and exclusive rewards. Read on to learn more about the return of Prestige and the valuable rewards up for grabs.

[b]Calling Card Challenges: [/b]Complete sets of Challenges in Multiplayer, Zombies, Campaign, and [i]Call of Duty: Warzone[/i] (Season 01) to unlock Calling Cards to equip to your Profile and Calling Card Showcase. It wouldn’t be a Black Ops game without hidden-criteria Dark Ops Challenges to discover and unlock. Chase after the “100 Percenter” Calling Cards in each mode for the ultimate Challenge bragging rights.

[b]Weapon Camos: [/b]The Weapon Camo grind has been overhauled in [i]Black Ops 6[/i] and is bigger than ever. Learn more about the new update to how you’ll be progressing through Camos on the quest to earn dynamic Dark Matter Camo in Multiplayer, Nebula Camo in Zombies, and the first ever [i]Call of Duty: Warzone[/i] Mastery Camo: Abyss (Season 01).

[b]Reticle Challenges:[/b] Customizable Reticles and Reticle Challenges return to Call of Duty in [i]Black Ops 6[/i]. Learn about how you’ll be unlocking and customizing Reticles in Multiplayer, Zombies, in [i]Call of Duty: Warzone[/i] (Season 01).

[b]Mastery Badges: [/b]All-new for [i]Black Ops 6[/i], every Weapon, Equipment, Field Upgrade, and Scorestreak in your Loadout has a set of Multiplayer and Zombies Mastery Badges to progress through as you master each piece of Gear. Use and Master each piece of content to unlock its Mastery Badge and Stat Tracker and prove your mettle by revealing your top three Badges in-game and in your Social Showcase.

[b]Medal Collection: [/b]View your top Medals and the accumulation of Medals you’ve earned in Multiplayer and Zombies. The Collection will also let you know what’s needed to unlock Medals you haven’t seen yet.
[h2]Level Unlocks[/h2]
[i]Global System (MP, RBZ, WZ)[/i]

[i]Barracks > Progression > Level Unlocks[/i]

[i]“Earn XP to progress through 55 Level Unlocks and gain access to Weapons, Equipment, Scorestreaks, Operators, and more.”[/i]
[h3]Level Unlocks: System Overview[/h3]
Here’s an overview of the main Progression System available for Multiplayer and Zombies at launch, and [i]Call of Duty: Warzone[/i] at the start of Season 01.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/4bd889261689479eacefb9bb49da8a33aceded3f.jpg[/img]

[b]Progression Access: [/b]Access Progression while in the Lobby via the Barracks tab at the top of the screen. Here, you’ll see a brief preview of your next Progression Reward and have the choice to dig into the “Progression” button for more info on Level Unlocks & Prestige.
[h3]Leveling Up: Level Unlocks[/h3]
[b][i]Player Levels 1-55[/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/d92dc7c293cff1c5d575206b59a1268869c19acf.jpg[/img]

You begin your [i]Black Ops 6[/i] Progression with a clear goal to accomplish: progress through Level Unlocks by climbing from “Private I” (Level 1) all the way to “Commander” (Level 55). This is achieved by earning XP in Multiplayer and Zombies (and in Season 01: [i]Call of Duty: Warzone[/i]). Earn XP by performing well, playing the Objective, earning Medals, and completing Challenges (more on Challenges later).

At every step from 1-55 you’ll unlock a variety of new content to use in your Loadouts in Multiplayer and Zombies:
[list]	[*]Weapons[/*]	[*]Lethal & Tactical Equipment[/*]	[*]Field Upgrades[/*]	[*]Scorestreaks[/*]	[*]Perks (Multiplayer Only)[/*]	[*]Wildcards (Multiplayer Only)[/*]	[*]Ammo Mods (Zombies Only)[/*]	[*]GobbleGums (Zombies Only)[/*][/list]
Additionally, [i]Black Ops 6[/i] players will unlock eight Base Operators and a selection of Emotes as they progress through the 1-55 Level Unlocks.

[b]Relocked Content Note: [/b]Both Operators and Emotes do not relock once you choose to embark on your Prestige journey. Consult the Prestige section of this blog for details.

[b]Black Ops 6 Items in Call of Duty: Warzone Note: [/b]Any compatible items from [i]Black Ops 6[/i] that you unlock during your Player Leveling will become available in [i]Call of Duty: Warzone [/i]at the start of Season 01, later this year.

[b]GobbleGums Note: [/b]All GobbleGums are unlocked from the start of the game. The ones listed in the Level Unlocks (1-55) are simply bonus GobbleGums that give you an extra one-time use item.
[h2]Level Unlocks: Player Level 1-55[/h2]
The linked table lists all the items you’ll unlock on your levelling journey from Level 1 (Private I) to Level 55 (Commander).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/21b37ae0599a93a1bfd1a6dff0eb3b34c5826e17.jpg[/img]

[url=https://www.callofduty.com/guides/blackops6/getting-started/call-of-duty-guides-black-ops-6-level-unlocks-player-level-1-55]Click here to view the entire Player Level journey![/url]
[h3]Level Unlocks: Highlights[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/754cab79b24160c4d7f5dee7b63c3ed009a54b49.jpg[/img]

The Launch Comms Blogs related to Weapons and Gear have tables showing the specific item type (Weapons, Field Upgrades, or Scorestreaks for example), so you can track unlockable content via Item rather than by Level (as shown in the Player Level table linked to previously). This becomes increasingly important as you decide which items to permanently unlock once you’ve chosen to Prestige.
[h2]Prestige[/h2][h2][i]Global System (MP, RBZ, WZ)[/i][/h2]
[i]Barracks > Progression > Prestige[/i]

Complete Level 55 and reach Max Level and you’ll face the option to take your grind to the next level: Welcome to [i]Black Ops 6[/i] Prestige. Not only has “Classic Prestige” returned in [i]Black Ops 6[/i], but it’s also the most rewarding version of Prestige that Call of Duty has ever seen – with rewards and each Prestige themed around a title in Black Ops history.
[h3]The Prestige Hub[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/3269d95cfc5f366c00d9c002bf03b3bf8037974e.jpg[/img]

Enter the Prestige Hub via the “Progression” button in the Barracks tab to view the full Prestige journey, preview rewards, and check in on your Prestige stats and Challenges.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/b5dd7a13b090b9f88d7e595f8fce05fcb303ac14.jpg[/img]

Select a Prestige, and you’ll be able to view all that Prestige’s rewards (and your progress through them depending on your current level).
[h3]Choosing to Prestige[/h3]
It wouldn’t be “Classic Prestige” if it wasn’t just a little...dangerous. Choosing to Prestige in past Call of Duty titles wasn’t without its risks, and that’s no different in [i]Black Ops 6[/i]. Make the choice to enter Prestige and you’ll get promoted to Prestige 1, but it will also be:
[list]	[*]Reset to Player Level 1.[/*]	[*]All Level Unlocks will be relocked and must be unlocked again, except for Base Operators, Emotes, and Zombies GobbleGums, as well as anything you Permanently Unlock (more on that later).[/*]	[*]Your Loadouts will be reset.[/*]	[*]Lifetime stats will remain viewable in the Combat Record, but your stats elsewhere in the game will only show stats for your current Prestige.[/*][/list]
However, the following items WILL NOT be relocked or reset:
[list]	[*]Weapon Progression, Camos, & Reticles.[/*]	[*]Weapon Builds - your favorite Weapon may be relocked but all the Builds you’ve created for it will be waiting for you when you reach the level needed to unlock it again.[/*]	[*]Challenge Progress & Unlocks.[/*]	[*]Store and Battle Pass Content.[/*]	[*]Operator and Emote Unlocks.[/*]	[*]Zombies GobbleGums.[/*][/list]
Additionally, any item you have a Blueprint or Skin for will remain Permanently Unlocked through Prestige. This means that if you have a Blueprint for the AS Val Assault Rifle, it won’t be relocked when you Prestige. The same goes for any Equipment, Field Upgrades, or Scorestreaks you possess Skins for.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/d20cbb905cb921ff2be1636679aa59a933d13b2d.jpg[/img]

When you choose to enter Prestige 1, you’ll immediately receive the following:
[list]	[*][b]Prestige 1 Icon:[/b] Your first Prestige icon, which slots into the center of your Level insignia for all players to see![/*]	[*]“Nacht Raider” Weaver Operator Skin.[/*]	[*]Access to the Prestige 1 Multiplayer and Zombies Calling Card Challenge Sets (more on Calling Card Challenges later in the blog).[/*]	[*]One Permanent Unlock (continue reading for more information).[/*][/list]
Additionally, as you start leveling through Prestige 1, you’ll unlock a unique Prestige reward every 10 Levels (at Level 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50).
[h3]Permanent Unlocks[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/c86a0e80454c2538d9c716f5ad58713be4960ed1.jpg[/img]

Each time you Prestige, you' acquire a “Permanent Unlock;”; an advantage with immense power that can only be used once! Here’s how this works:
[list]	[*]You can use it to unlock a single item of your choice within the Player Levels.[/*]	[*]You obtain a total of ten Permanent Unlocks, one per Prestige.[/*]	[*]Once you complete Prestige 10, Permanent Unlocks provide no further function as your Level Unlocks Progression becomes fully available once you’ve entered Prestige Master.[/*][/list]
[b]Permanent Unlock Example:[/b] If you don’t want to wait until you’ve progressed back to Level 49 to unlock the Kompakt 92 SMG, you can utilize the Permanent Unlock at any time to gain immediate access to the weapon.

You’re encouraged to make strategic choices about which items to permanently unlock, so you have more control over your gameplay experience by ensuring access to your preferred gear.

[b]Prestige Rewards:[/b] As previously noted, once you’ve Prestiged, you gain access to earn otherwise-unobtainable Prestige Rewards, Prestige Challenges, and an increased XP bonus for completing each day’s three Daily Challenges.

[b]Stats Reset:[/b] Your stats – such as your current Elimination/Death Ratio – start fresh every time you Prestige. However, you can always view your Lifetime Career stats in the Barracks > Stats > Combat Record menu.
[h3]Prestige Leveling[/h3]
If you took the plunge and entered Prestige, your level resets to Level 1, Prestige 1. The date you entered Prestige is recorded, and you receive an instant reward. Now, as you level up and re-unlock the Level rewards, you also unlock the Prestige rewards as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/d5ac8daecdb3e12c17a5ffe0f358dd4604a8a6fc.jpg[/img]

[b]Welcome to Black Ops History! [/b]In [i]Black Ops 6[/i], each Prestige is themed around a game in Black Ops history, featuring a variety of rewards inspired by and paying homage to moments and elements found in each Black Ops title. For example, Prestige 1 features rewards inspired by the first game in the Black Ops timeline: 2008’s [i]Call of Duty: World at War[/i], the origin of Zombies in Call of Duty.
[h3]Prestige 1: Rewards Showcase[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/3c2df09914fc4cf6b10812dc0f886c67fa1a2e31.jpg[/img]

For the veterans that fondly remember the very first time Zombies appeared in a Call of Duty, as well as players who crave some of the coolest exclusive earnable items around, Prestige 1’s rewards have you covered. Here’s a fully unredacted look:
[h3]Instant Reward: Prestige 1 Icon[/h3]
Your first Prestige icon is animated and takes the form of a World at War soldier, but with a menacing, zombified appearance.
[h3]Instant Reward: “Nacht Raider” Weaver Operator Skin[/h3]
Inspired by the origins of Zombies from [i]Call of Duty: World at War[/i], this Zombified Weaver is clad in tattered and bloody WWII soldier fatigues, with glowing eyes.
[h3]Prestige 1, Level 10: “Der Riese” Loading Screen & Social Wallpaper[/h3]
Return to Group 935’s base of operations with this artwork inspired by the Der Riese Zombies map.
[h3]Prestige 1, Level 20: “Perk-A-Cola” GobbleGum Pack (Premium-only*)[/h3]
A one-hour XP Token plus a GobbleGum Pack, ready for use in [i]Black Ops 6[/i] Zombies. Expect the following GobbleGums in this Pack:
[list]	[*][b]Perkaholic:[/b] Gives the player all available Perks.[/*]	[*][b]On the House:[/b] Spawns a Random Perk Power-Up.[/*]	[*][b]Soda Fountain:[/b] The next Perk purchased gives an additional random Perk.[/*]	[*][b]Who’s Keeping Score:[/b] Spawns a Double Points Power-Up.[/*]	[*][b]Stock Option:[/b] Ammo is taken from the player's stockpile instead of their weapon's magazine.[/*][/list][h3]Prestige 1, Level 30: “Zombie Breach” Animated Emblem[/h3]
A yellow-eyed undead shambler breaks through some hastily constructed defenses in this Animated Emblem.
[h3]Prestige 1, Level 40: “Insta-kill Power-Up” Charm[/h3]
A gleaming gold skull symbolizing the powerful Zombies Insta-Kill Power-Up.
[h3]Prestige 1, Level 50: “Teddy is a Liar” C9 Blueprint (SMG, Premium-only*)[/h3]
Featuring the eerie "Teddy is a Liar" Easter egg from [i]Call of Duty: World at War Zombies[/i] and inspired by an infamous submachine gun from [i]World at War[/i], this Blueprint will add a touch of mystery and nostalgia to your arsenal.

*[b]BO6 Required Rewards: [/b]Though the [i]Black Ops 6[/i] Prestige Progression System is global across Multiplayer, Zombies, and [i]Call of Duty: Warzone[/i], players who own [i]Black Ops 6[/i] will have access to additional rewards not available to free-to-play [i]Call of Duty: Warzone[/i] players. [i]Call of Duty: Warzone[/i] players who decide to purchase [i]Black Ops 6[/i] will instantly unlock any “BO6 Required” Prestige rewards they previously earned but did not receive.
[h3]Future Prestiges: Rewards Teaser[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/ea4e96248c820a8f590f5d45f53a5cd0afef7731.jpg[/img]

Should you decide to continue your epic journey and climb through all ten Prestiges, expect a similar level of rewards and reminiscence. The previous image shows only a few of the additional rewards to earn.
[h3]Prestige 3, Level 50: “My Name is…” Payne Operator Skin[/h3]
Operator Callum Payne has become a mysterious figure cloaked in a hood, evoking the intense legacy of Alex Mason and Victor Reznov from [i]Call of Duty: Black Ops[/i].
[h3]Prestige 4, Level 50: “Atomic Commando” XM4 Assault Rifle Blueprint[/h3]
A vibrant and nostalgic design, capturing the colorful essence of the iconic Nuketown map from the original [i]Call of Duty: Black Ops[/i].
[h3]Prestige 5, Level 50: “Absolute Loss” Toro Operator Skin[/h3]
Operator Toro wears a jacket infused with symbols of rage, embodying the fury and vengeance of Raul Menendez against the Black Ops team in [i]Call of Duty: Black Ops II[/i].
[h3]Prestige 6, Level 50: “Robot Abomination” SWAT 556 Marksman Rifle Blueprint[/h3]
Inspired by the legendary giant robot from [i]Call of Duty: Black Ops II [/i]Zombies, this weapon evokes both immense power and mystery.
[h3]Prestige 7, Level 50: “Specialist Fan” Maya Operator Skin[/h3]
Maya showcases her love for [i]Call of Duty: Black Ops III[/i] with a mixture of gear inspired by the Specialist Operator Battery, and a shirt proudly displaying the [i]Black Ops III[/i] logo.
[h2]Become a Legend: Prestige Master Levels[/h2]
There are 10 Prestiges in [i]Call of Duty: Black Ops 6[/i]. If you’re dedicated enough to complete all of them, you’ll automatically graduate into Prestige Master and enter the final phase of [i]Black Ops 6[/i] Career Progression. In Prestige Master, your Level rises above 55 for the first time as you are now able to climb up all the way to Level 1,000 and gain additional rewards in the process.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/692dac647d6ed6a75b9bd1e088dd32d593d15b13.jpg[/img]

Still cloaked in mystery, the rewards for ascending all the way to Prestige Master are well worth the grind. Who will be the first to unlock theirs?
[h3]Prestige Master Instant Reward: “Sitting Bull Reborn” Marshall Operator Skin[/h3]
Marshall rocks an outfit inspired by the cover art of [i]Black Ops 6[/i], capturing the essence of the ‘sitting bull’ pose and the 90s military era.
[h3]Prestige Master Level 90: “Classified Arsenal” AMES 85 Animated Blueprint[/h3]
Redacted bits cover the weapon in a striking pattern, symbolizing the covert and secretive world of [i]Black Ops 6[/i].
[h3]Prestige Master: Legacy Prestige Icons and More[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/8b3a85c3bc252df3b5f0006a88915dfa394edfbf.jpg[/img]

[i]The Legacy Prestige 1 Icons. Can you name all the games they first appeared in?[/i]

Players who reach Prestige Master Level 100 will gain the ability to customize their Prestige via access to Legacy Prestige Icons from past Call of Duty titles. Equipping one of these Legacy Prestige Icons replaces your Prestige Master icon and changes the way your Prestige Master status appears to other players anywhere it’s seen in-and-out of game. At Prestige Master Level 100, access to Legacy Prestige 1 icons becomes available. From this point forward, gain access to a new set of Legacy Prestige Icons every 100 Prestige Master Levels:
[list]	[*]Prestige Master Level 100: Equip any Legacy Prestige 1 Icon[/*]	[*]Prestige Master Level 200: Equip any Legacy Prestige 2 Icon[/*]	[*]Prestige Master Level 300: Equip any Legacy Prestige 3 Icon[/*]	[*]Prestige Master Level 400: Equip any Legacy Prestige 4 Icon[/*]	[*]Prestige Master Level 500: Equip any Legacy Prestige 5 Icon[/*]	[*]Prestige Master Level 600: Equip any Legacy Prestige 6 Icon[/*]	[*]Prestige Master Level 700: Equip any Legacy Prestige 7 Icon[/*]	[*]Prestige Master Level 800: Equip any Legacy Prestige 8 Icon[/*]	[*]Prestige Master Level 900: Equip any Legacy Prestige 9 Icon[/*]	[*]Prestige Legend (Level 1,000): Equip any Legacy Prestige 10 icon (or above)[/*][/list]
Prestige Master players who’ve reached Level 100 or above can select a Legacy Prestige Icon via the “Customize” menu in the Barracks.

[b]Become a Legend:[/b] As you reach the zenith of your [i]Black Ops 6[/i] career and become a “Prestige Legend” at the game’s maximum Level (1,000), expect additional, Classified rewards for your incredible progress, only unlocked and redacted when you reach Level 1,000.
[h2]Calling Card Challenges[/h2]
[i]Global System (SP, MP, RBZ, WZ)[/i]

[i]Barracks > Challenges > Calling Card Challenge Menu[/i]
[h3]Calling Cards: System Overview[/h3]
[b]Recap[/b]: Calling Card Challenges are back in [i]Black Ops 6[/i], with over 450 Calling Cards available to be earned by completing a variety of Challenges in Campaign, Multiplayer, Zombies and (in Season 01) [i]Call of Duty: Warzone.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/878e7dfd98d465acaa83e28307b2c9fce8385a6e.jpg[/img]

Access Calling Card Challenges via the “Challenges” button in the Barracks tab. Here you can view Challenges for all four modes, split out into different categories:
[list]	[*]Career.[/*]	[*]Battle Hardened.[/*]	[*]Prestige (Multiplayer, Zombies and [i]Call of Duty: Warzone[/i] only).[/*]	[*]Dark Ops.[/*][/list]

notes.title: Black Ops 6:Weapons detail, part 1
notes.notes:
[b][u]Armaments Intel: Primary, Secondary, and Melee Weapons (MP, RBZ, WZ)[/u][/b]

At launch, expect [i]Black Ops 6[/i] to offer an exceptional arsenal of 33 different armaments to utilize, including 12 weapons all new to the franchise. As you begin to build your favorite Loadouts within a streamlined Weapons menu, and prepare for the Weapon Leveling to come, it’s worth considering the different types of weaponry available to you, how they unlock, and a closer look into a more accessible Gunsmith.

[b]Primary Weapons (25)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/589b600a39a8dc251528608a4680df6d596ae42f.jpg[/img]

Your main and usually hardest-hitting weapon utilized for most of your time in combat. Expect a varied and interesting selection of weapons in each category, as well as the individual Attachments for each Primary Weapon, which are – except for some Optics – unlocked as you level each weapon up. The Gunsmith is available for all Primary Weapons. Run the Wildcard “Overkill” if you wish to equip a second Primary Weapon in the Secondary Weapon slot. Choose from:
[list]	[*]Assault Rifles (7)[/*]	[*]SMGs (6)[/*]	[*]Shotguns (2)[/*]	[*]LMGs (3)[/*]	[*]Marksman Rifles (4)[/*]	[*]Sniper Rifles (3)[/*][/list]
[b]Secondary Weapons (6)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/e95cac091aeab2a131e86976c266fa1b29731af0.jpg[/img]

Your back-up weapon, used in emergency or context-specific situations. These weapons are carried in addition to the Primary Weapon you pick, and more adept Operators tend to choose a Secondary Weapon that complements their Primary Weapon in some way. Running the Overkill Wildcard will allow players to equip two Primary weapons, as well. The Gunsmith is available for Secondary Weapons. Choose from:
[list]	[*]Pistols (4)[/*]	[*]Launchers (2)[/*][/list]
[b]Melee Weapons (2)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/12cff94f1e8f44ecb374a4ae21b658f4cb2b73b0.jpg[/img]

Your third weapon is a close-quarters armament with no ranged ordnance. Bring out your Melee weapon using the same key or button press as Melee (for controllers, this is the Right thumbstick). Tap this for a gun butt melee. Hold to bring out your Melee weapon, which will remain equipped until you swap back to your Primary or Secondary. There’s also the Weapon Cycle setting (accessed via Controller > Combat > Dedicated Melee Weapon Activation > Hold Melee/Weapon Cycle), which allows players to use the weapon swap button to cycle between Primary, Secondary, and Melee weapons if they so choose. The Gunsmith is available for Melee Weapons (Cosmetics only). Choose from:
[list]	[*]Knife (1)[/*]	[*]Baseball Bat (1)[/*][/list]
[b]Player Levels: Weapon Unlock Criteria[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/dd38985e5ade317b91f997e7fc03760a0f777f19.jpg[/img]

All the launch weaponry in [i]Black Ops 6[/i] have specific unlock criteria, and this is related to your Player Progression (accessed via the Progression tab in the Barracks Menu). Gain Experience Points as you play matches to level up, then unlock weapons once you reach a particular Player Progression Level, as shown in the following table. Note that one weapon from each type or class is always immediately available in Default Loadouts and the rest are unlocked as you level up. Look for more information on Player Leveling later in this blog, and full details on all the Player Level Unlocks in the Launch Comms: Progression Blog.

[b]Perk Notes: [/b]Equip the following to affect the use of your weaponry in a variety of different ways:
[list]	[*][b]Gung-Ho [/b](Enforcer) reduces movement penalties when reloading or using Equipment and allows reloading while Tactical Sprinting.[/*]	[*][b]Dexterity[/b] (Enforcer) reduces weapon motion while jumping, sliding, and diving.[/*]	[*][b]Scavenger [/b](Enforcer) allows ammo resupply from downed enemies.[/*]	[*][b]Bruiser[/b] (Enforcer) enables Melee kills to replenish health and earn extra score.[/*]	[*][b]Tracker [/b](Recon) enables auto-pinging enemies when you ADS.[/*]	[*][b]Cold-Blooded [/b](Recon) prevents thermal optics from targeting you.[/*]	[*][b]Fast Hands [/b](Strategist) allows you to swap weapons faster.[/*][/list]
[b]Wildcard Notes: [/b]Equip the following to affect the use of your weaponry in a variety of different ways:
[list]	[*][b]Overkill[/b] allows you to equip any non-melee weapon in Primary and Secondary slots.[/*]	[*][b]Gunfighter [/b]allows you to receive three extra Attachment points for your Primary Weapon.[/*][/list]
[b][u]Primary Weapons (25)[/u][/b]

[b]Assault Rifles (7)[/b]

[b]Attachment Types: [/b]Optic, Muzzle*, Barrel, Underbarrel, Magazine, Rear Grip, Stock, Laser, Fire Mods.

[i](*AS VAL has no Muzzle Attachment)[/i]

Medium range Primary Weapons. Average mobility, hard-hitting and versatile due to the available attachment options. Usually full-auto, with iron sights and ADS options for Optics.

[b]XM4[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/905e9124d181632e74d9d86296e012b98e3eb1e4.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 30[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked Immediately

Full-auto assault rifle. A well-rounded weapon with average accuracy, mobility, and power among its counterparts.

[b]AK-74[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/2061de3127def609b156cf9f9b632cad822ed38e.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 30[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 10

Full-auto assault rifle. Imposing firepower with high damage at mid-to-long range balanced by a slower rate of fire and heavier recoil.

[b]AMES 85[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/4862e6d842dd681088f30b692f56e059214ab225.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 30[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 19

Full-auto assault rifle. Impressive accuracy and a suitable rate of fire make this an excellent weapon for mid to long range engagements.

[b]GPR 91[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/3fdcf2b4de89c138d1c58be2adb6b2215f0d918a.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 30[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 28

Full-auto assault rifle. What this rifle lacks in raw power, it makes up for in spades with best-in-class handling and a decent rate of fire.

[b]MODEL L[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/a5872ba368753d0c07fcc734ba13bb94f2dde8ae.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 30[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 40

Full-auto assault rifle. Slow-firing and controllable with respectable damage, the Model L shines in calculated engagements at mid-range.

[b]GOBLIN MK 2[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/78bc7f0b25dd3c787ca5bc8b5091568e45b2cc89.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 4[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 20[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 46

Semi-auto assault rifle. The Goblin Mk2 excels at short to mid ranges where its operator can take full advantage of its handling and impressive rate of fire.

[b]AS VAL[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/f9b2a008460b26ee51b1bd7639e80d03eb0dcd9d.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 5[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 20[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 55

Full-auto assault rifle. Leads the way in stealth while remaining suitable for urban combat through its integrated suppressor and improved mobility.

[b]SMGS (6)[/b]

[b]Attachment Types: [/b]Optic, Muzzle, Barrel, Underbarrel*, Magazine, Rear Grip, Stock, Laser, Fire Mods.

[i](*PP-919 has no Underbarrel Attachment)[/i]

Medium to short-range Primary Weaponry, with good mobility and handling, though not quite as accurate as an AR. Iron sights and ADS options are available for Optics.

[b]C9[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/3d4c2432b32e6728bfe431ff45416197a90a776e.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 4[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 30[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked Immediately

Full-auto submachine gun. The C9 is a well-balanced weapon that performs reliably in all close to mid-range situations.

[b]KSV[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/e7c5e9e2cadaa1bf44266fc304fdbcb6697bbb3e.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 4[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 30[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 7

Full-auto submachine gun. Fast to aim with manageable recoil and good damage. Perfect for a dexterous operator seeking broad proficiency.

[b]TANTO .22[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/8c5e5abfdb33fb11e9df192f9d23a5500b747341.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 4[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 30[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 16

Full-auto submachine gun. Slow-firing, but hard-hitting, the Tanto .22 is an easy-to-handle SMG with impressive mid-range performance.

[b]PP-919[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/28218c35c101c60c8d861dde97825bbe24eff623.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 2[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 64[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 37

Full-auto submachine gun. The PP-919 has the highest ammo counts in class, at the cost of some mobility and fire rate.

[b]JACKAL PDW[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/294ac5b3dbf776d0269c0101597199a7ee4c051d.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 4[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 30[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 43

Full-auto submachine gun. Great mobility and handling make this an easy choice for operators who aggressively seek CQB engagements.

[b]KOMPAKT 92[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/45baa20e4c18804415717ef65bec7343c317226c.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 4[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 30[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 49

Full-auto submachine gun. Chambered in 9mm with the fastest fire rate in class, the Kompakt 92 excels in close-range encounters.

[b]Shotguns (2)[/b]

[b]Attachment Types: [/b]Optic, Muzzle, Barrel, Underbarrel, Magazine*, Rear Grip*, Stock, Laser, Fire Mods.

[i](*ASG-89 only)[/i]

Advantageous at very close ranges, offering iron sights and ADS via Optics, and with correct Attachments, the ability to spray. Incredible firepower at the expense of range and accuracy.

[b]Marine SP[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/699cc43c856990f1189efe2afb997d5e0e05d6a3.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 4[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 6[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked Immediately

Pump-action shotgun. Powerful and versatile with a short cycling time that allows for rapid target acquisition. Hand loaded with one-shot kill potential in close quarters.

[b]ASG-89[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/bbee43f53f13f4cc364cf3f575c81d494e03c3bf.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 4[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 6[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 31

Semi-automatic shotgun. Capable of taking down multiple targets in quick succession thanks to its decent magazine size and solid rate of fire.

[b]LMGs (3)[/b]

[b]Attachment Types: [/b]Optic, Muzzle, Barrel, Underbarrel, Magazine, Rear Grip, Stock, Laser, Fire Mods.

Primary Weapons with increased ammo capacity and a focus on medium to long-range takedowns. Iron sights and ADS available via Optics. Though Accuracy, Mobility and Handling are sacrificed (compared to ARs), this is balanced by impressive fire rates and fast sustained fire capabilities.

[b]PU-21[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/e1b1d1e19c1233a6414a08fc9e51ed536e871a3e.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 75[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked Immediately

Full-auto light machine gun. Deceptively lightweight and easy to aim with high damage. Rewards vigilance and careful recoil control.

[b]XMG[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/6e8232945d6c7ddcd55798a2ce653a686f1122f4.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 100[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 13

Full-auto light machine gun. Belt-fed with best-in-class ammo capacity, the XMG has a slower fire rate, but powerful sustained fire accuracy.

[b]GPMG-7[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/64e444ec2556d3e6fdce9bc6f8ba7eda087e57f5.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 50[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 52

Full-auto light machine gun. Unparalleled ability to quickly neutralize threats thanks to a blistering fire rate and suitable long-range damage.

[b]Marksman Rifles (4)[/b]

[b]Attachment Types: [/b]Optic, Muzzle, Barrel, Underbarrel, Magazine, Rear Grip, Stock, Laser, Fire Mods.

Favoring an Operator with over-average skill, these burstor semi-auto Primary Weapons are optimal at medium to long ranges. ADS or iron sights available for Optics. Projectiles are hard-hitting and accuracy counts.

[b]SWAT 5.56[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/f2bf80107a5b501ff9b602c5ba425dfae90a7e55.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 30[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked Immediately

Three-round burst DMR. The Swat 5.56 pairs strong stopping power with a fast burst cooldown for excellence at medium ranges.

[b]Tsarkov 7.62[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/edae8a7410fcc8eaac509ed72706fcdaae4ec82f.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 20[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 22

Semi-auto DMR. The Tsarkov 7.62 sacrifices only some power in exchange for excellent handling, making it lethal in the hands of an accurate and mobile Operator.

[b]AEK-973[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/06c575bd781c7f5083e576b4c0fde93cf597b497.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 30[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 34

Three-round burst DMR. Great stability and a fast rate of fire within each burst allows the AEK-973 to land multiple shots on target even at long ranges.

[b]DM-10[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/c3e7c1b1a256eeefbb0b38ce649e758273a6b47e.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 20[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 43

Semi-auto DMR. Best in class stability and power make this the ideal marksman weapon for mid to long range engagements.

[b]Sniper Rifles (3)[/b]

[b]Attachment Types: [/b]Optic, Muzzle, Barrel, Magazine, Comb, Stock, Laser, Fire Mods, Stock Pad*.

[i](*LW3A1 Frostline only)[/i]

Normally set up to take down targets at extremely long ranges, these Primary Weapons favor ADS over iron sights when using Optics. Low mobility, and favoring a stable, patient Operator with a steady aim. Extremely high Firepower indicates one-shot takedown potential.

[b]LW3A1 Frostline[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/3238182ae1d27270ec2e23be03b4b394937a0f92.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 4[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 5[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked Immediately

Bolt-action sniper rifle. The LW3A1 Frostline has decent rate of fire and handling speeds, but substantial recoil. One shot kill to the head, upper chest, and upper arms. Hold the Left Thumbstick while ADS to steady.

[b]SVD[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/ea47e3a507a53c6d50d8cb94d12795df4b94528f.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 10[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 25

Semi-auto sniper rifle. Gas-operated Soviet sniper with modest vertical kick. Capable of landing precise follow-up shots. One skill kill to the head. Hold the Left Thumbstick while ADS to steady.

[b]LR 7.62[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/86baa8141ee5119099156860265c9591a39c6a3d.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 4[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 5[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 49

Bolt-action sniper rifle. The LR 7.62 delivers high damage with minimal recoil and slower handling. One shot kill to the head, chest, and arms. Hold the Left Thumbstick while ADS to steady.

[b][u]Secondary Weapons (6)[/u][/b]

[b]Pistols (4)[/b]

[b]Attachment Types: [/b]Optic, Muzzle, Barrel, Magazine, Rear Grip, Stock, Laser, Fire Mods.

Full or semi-auto Secondary Weapons, these excel at closer-range takedowns. Iron sights or ADS is available via Optics. Quick to swap to during a fight, and worth considering when finishing off an opponent.

[b]9mm PM[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/0edbb09eec8d99ddf1da0d32746e9a361d700019.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 10[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked Immediately

Semi-auto pistol. With a decent rate of fire and standard handling, the 9mm PM is a masterclass in reliability and the easy choice for all close-quarter engagements.

[b]Grekhova[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/7c7b984428370968fe4535946a45f96822cee079.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 20[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 13

Full-auto pistol. Surprising accuracy combined with a fast rate of fire offsets the lower damage and smaller effective range of the Grekhova.

[b]GS45[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/7113b753a83c2df64ba66d5d931a6b0b7c4be550.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 10[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked at Player Level 28

Semi-auto pistol. The GS45’s .45 Auto rounds make this sidearm unmatched in close range stopping power.

[b]Stryder .22[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/1f0eeeb30d80d88d95e7a42acd2b71a9979983b5.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 2[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 30[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 40

Semi-auto pistol. The Stryder .22 excels at finishing off damaged opponents in the heat of combat thanks to its fast semi-automatic rate of fire and best in class handling.

[b]Launchers (2)[/b]

[b]Attachment Types: [/b]None.

Available in lock-on or free-fire variants, these bulky Secondary Weapons are useful for clearing groups of Operators, or against vehicles or technology such as Scorestreaks. Single load, with a sizeable bulk.

[b]CIGMA 2B[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/340024a6ae7cf77ef5796d9de2a6f4942d53eb18.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 2[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 1[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked Immediately

Lock-on capable launcher. Can lock onto enemy Scorestreaks and vehicles. Fires a high-explosive 110-mm warhead for massive damage.

[b]HE-1[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/4e08420c2a976b5ef560e0d9908e5e9162027f7f.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 3[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 1[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 19

Free-fire rocket launcher. Fires a high-explosive 110-mm warhead for massive damage.

[b]Melee Weapons (2)[/b]

[b]Attachment Types: [/b]None.

Close-quarter battle (CQB) combat armaments offering vicious damage potential and arguably the fastest Mobility of any armament. No range capabilities.

[b]Knife[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/44d6bb8c9af42c7173cf99b4e2b877214815820e.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 1[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 1[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked Immediately

One hit kill. Military-issue tactical knife well-suited for CQC scenarios where stealth, speed, and lethality are required.

[b]Baseball Bat[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/41ff4164f8382eecf31bb182746b360fb3c250ff.jpg[/img]

[b]MAGS: 1[/b]

[b]MAG SIZE: 1[/b]

[b]Available: [/b]Unlocked at Player Level 52

Two-hit kill. The aluminum bat is light enough for quick swings and heavy enough to inflict serious, blunt trauma on victims.

[b][u]Weapon Menus: Loadouts, Gunsmith, and Attachments (MP, RBZ, WZ)[/u][/b]

[b]Loadouts[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/d6f4e3fb0ef5f1d57c1949f20e127be3533e8004.jpg[/img]

Your Loadout screen is familiar yet updated. Menus are mainly vertical, and the slots within a Loadout involve choosing armaments that differ slightly depending on the Mode you’re playing:
[list]	[*][b]Multiplayer: [/b]Choose three types of weapons (Primary, Secondary, Melee), three types of Equipment (Tactical, Lethal, and an MP-only Field Upgrade), three Perks (MP), an optional Specialty related to your Perk choice, and a Wildcard.[/*]	[*][b]Zombies:[/b] Choose two types of weapons (Primary or Secondary, and Melee), three types of Equipment (Tactical, Lethal, and a Zombies-only Field Upgrade), and a GobbleGum Pack (Zombies only).[/*]	[*]This blog details the first three Loadout slots (the Primary, Secondary, and Melee Weapons).[/*]	[*]You can add Loadouts, creating a maximum of ten.[/*]	[*]You can set one Loadout as your favorite. This Loadout acts as your default spawn class in games, and your Operator will carry the Primary Weapon in the Lobby.[/*]	[*]You can Rename, Duplicate, or Delete any Loadout.[/*][/list]
[b]Content Unlocks[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/d874860a6b88e065ca0fd34f1a1889be0abf1ce5.jpg[/img]

You begin your [i]Black Ops 6[/i] journey with most of your Loadout items locked. There’s a wide variety of functional content to unlock on your journey through the 55 Player Levels. Every time you level up, be sure to check the Barracks > Progression > Level Unlocks menu (shown above) to ensure you’re aware of the unlocks you now have available to you. Expect between one and three unlocks per level.

Each specific unlock box in this menu has the game mode it applies to, or simply the BO6 logo if the item is available in all modes. The following type of content is unlockable, and usually adds to your existing item pools:

Loadouts (Default) (MP)

Loadouts (Custom) (MP)

Weapons (Primary) (MP, RBZ, WZ)

Weapons (Secondary) (MP, RBZ, WZ)

Weapons (Melee) (MP, RBZ, WZ)

Tacticals (MP, RBZ, WZ)

Lethals (MP, RBZ, WZ)

Field Upgrades (MP, WZ)

Field Upgrades (RBZ)

Perks (MP)

Wildcards (MP)

Scorestreaks (MP, RBZ, WZ)

Ammo Mods (RBZ)

GobbleGums (RBZ)

Operators (MP, RBZ, WZ)

Emotes (MP, RBZ, WZ)

Features (MP, RBZ, WZ)

Expect a full and thorough overview of how all your items unlock in the [b][u]Launch Comms Blog 5: Progression.[/u][/b]

[b]The Firing Range[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/644efd1c97d01c4132a353c865ad09f81c1025c0.jpg[/img]

A familiar location to test your equipped Loadout weapons is available, and this comes with a few additions to help you continuously adjust a weapon build until you’re happy with it. Expect to utilize the following:
[list]	[*]Practice dummies to shoot at, at 10-, 25-, and 50-meter intervals.[/*]	[*]Dummies can have 0, 1, 2, or 3 Armor Plates added to them.[/*]	[*]You have almost limitless ammunition.[/*]	[*]The upper-left corner features a target elimination tracker, an accuracy tracker, and a damage tracker.[/*]	[*]A toggle feature allows you to optionally activate a Moving Target dummy, or a Recoil metal plate.[/*]	[*][b]Toggle Feature: Moving Target:[/b] A dummy drops down from the ceiling on a conveyor belt, and automatically moves back through the range as you connect with it using your weapon. Once you hit it at maximum range, it moves back to its initial position, and the process can be repeated.[/*]	[*][b]Toggle Feature: Recoil Target: [/b]A metal plate hangs from the ceiling around seven meters from your booth, allowing you to fire your weapon and view the bullet spread.[/*][/list]

notes.title: Black Ops 6:Weapons detail, part 2
notes.notes:
[b]Global Weapon Builds[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/c3065d292a845448ed282361873cc88b062c95cb.jpg[/img]

Whether you’re playing [i]Black Ops 6[/i] Multiplayer, Round Based Zombies or [i]Call of Duty®: Warzone™[/i] (at Season 1), you can utilize a weapon build you’ve created across all three game modes. This time-saving innovation allows you to make a change to any Build or Blueprint in any game, and it permeates out everywhere the gun is equipped. Here’s an example of how this works.

Let’s say you want to create an AMES 85 Variant. In the Loadout Menu (MP, RBZ, or WZ though MP is shown above), simply complete the following:
[list]	[*]Select the weapon in question and go to “+ Create New Build.”[/*]	[*]Choose the Base Weapon, or any of the Blueprints you’ve collected, as the basis of your new Weapon Build.[/*]	[*]Enter the Gunsmith, and perfect your weapon by adding Attachments, Cosmetics, and testing the weapon out in the Firing Range.[/*]	[*]Move back to the Custom Loadout screen, where your weapon has a default name, and select “Build Options.”[/*]	[*]Rename your weapon (you can also duplicate or reset it, too).[/*]	[*]Your weapon is automatically saved. Now, when you access the Loadout Menus in your other game modes (in this example, RBZ or WZ), the weapon, along with the Attachments, Cosmetics, and name, appears.[/*]	[*]All builds are saved within the menu of the individual weapon type.[/*][/list]
[b][u]Gunsmith: Attachments Intel (MP, RBZ, WZ)[/u][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/36753647a36dd24085084a07beed1ea26ca0ff44.jpg[/img]

[b]Recap: [/b]As detailed at Call of Duty: NEXT, the focus for [i]Black Ops 6[/i] is to condense and streamline Attachments so you can easily understand the bonuses when it comes to utilizing the Gunsmith. Here are some of the changes:
[list]	[*][b]Gaining the Advantage:[/b] Attachments almost always come with a benefit (Pro), and not a detriment (Con), so you know you’re creating a weapon more potent than the base version.[/*]	[*][b]Optics for All... :[/b] Almost all Optic Attachments are shared across all weapons in a Weapon Class. For example, unlock the Red Dot Sight with a SMG and you’ll be able to equip it to all SMGs in the Weapon Class.[/*]	[*][b]...Everything Else is Unique:[/b] All other Attachment Types – Muzzle, Barrel, Underbarrel, Magazine, Rear Grip, Stock, Laser, and Fire Mods – are unique to the weapon in question in terms of unlocking and usage.[/*]	[*][b]Getting Specific:[/b] Instead of having a weapon function – such as ADS speed – being affected by multiple attachments that are difficult to keep track of, they are related to a single Attachment type.	[list]		[*]For example, equipping a “Rear Grip” Attachment will always improve your handling, and the grip you choose will boost a unique combination of handling stats (to Sprint to Fire Speed, Slide to Fire Speed, Dive to Fire Speed, ADS Speed, or a combination thereof). All the different grips are designed to improve the weapon’s potency, not reduce it.[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Information is Power:[/b] The net result of this new system is that it allows players to make informed weapon-building decisions easily and create effective Builds without constantly needing looking up “meta” builds online.[/*][/list]
[b]Details Matter:[/b] Don’t mistake this streamlining as “dumbing down” the Gunsmith, as your Firepower, Accuracy, Handling, and Mobility statistics can also be seen in an expanded view, with individual elements like Reload Quickness, Recoil Gun Kick, and Bullet Velocity all available to compare in granular detail.

[b]Attachment Types[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/cda5464587ae345526bc4b54377d2c199f1894d4.jpg[/img]

As always, Attachments are divided into types, and each type provides a basic advantage when placed onto your weapon, along with specific additional benefits based on the unique nature of each specific part. The following table shows the 11 different Attachment Types available at launch, and which Weapon Types utilize them:

[b]Key: [/b]The preceding table has the following information related to Weapon and Attachment Types, as follows:

[b]YES: [/b]Every weapon within the Weapon Type uses this Attachment Type.

[b]SOME: [/b]Most, but not all, of the Weapon Type uses this Attachment Type.

[b]NO: [/b]This Attachment Type is not available for the Weapon Type.

For example, the “Comb” Attachment Type is only available on Sniper Rifles.

[b]Note: [/b]Attachment Type Descriptions are detailed throughout the rest of this Blog, so you know what each one does. See below.

[b]Five Attachments Per Weapon. Eight if You’re a Gunfighter[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/baeda142c0f1f4acadea7c9f8e1c8bdc4da96f10.jpg[/img]

Along with the weapon’s current level, the Attachments Menu also indicates the number of Attachments you can place, and have placed, on your weapon. These are known as “Attachment Points.”
[list]	[*]There are five points available, for Assault Rifles, SMGs, Shotguns, LMGs, Marksman Rifles, Sniper Rifles, and Pistols.[/*]	[*]You can pick none, or up to five Attachment Points, though the more slots used, the better the weapon is likely to perform.[/*]	[*]Each weapon type has more available Attachment types than points. For example, you can choose up to five points when building out an SMG, but there are nine Attachment Types.[/*]	[*]Launchers and Melee Weapons do not have Attachment points.[/*]	[*]You can increase the number of Attachment Points from five to eight by selecting the Gunfighter Wildcard, available when you reach Player Level 33.[/*][/list]
[b]Attachments: Main Statistics and Details[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/3d51f47fc2b96724e7b552c99e52740b333afadc.jpg[/img]

[b]Four Main Statistics: [/b]Each weapon has a baseline value related to one of four key attributes: Firepower, Accuracy, Mobility, and Handling. These are each represented by a grey bar in the bottom-right corner of the Gunsmith Attachments Menu. In each case, the higher the value, the better. As you’d expect, some weapons are intrinsically more proficient when it comes to one or more of these statistics. For example, a Sniper Rifle has the best “Firepower” of all weapon types.

Each aspect of a weapon’s performance is related to these four statistics:
[list]	[*][b]Firepower: [/b]The fire rate, damage, range, and firing ping on the Mini-Map.[/*]	[*][b]Accuracy: [/b]The minimum and maximum Hip Fire Spread, Recoil Gun Kick, Horizontal and Vertical Recoil, bullet velocity, and Flinch Resistance.[/*]	[*][b]Mobility: [/b]The Movement Speed (Crouch, normal, Sprint, and ADS).[/*]	[*][b]Handling: [/b]Reload quickness (both with rounds and empty), ADS Speed, Sprint to Fire Time, and Weapon Swap Speed.[/*][/list]
Every time you add an attachment to your weapon, it affects one (or more) of the above statistics. In [i]Black Ops 6[/i], adding an attachment usually grants you more pronounced advantages (“Pros”), and limited disadvantages (“Cons”) compared to the weapon without the attachment fitted.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/87b2c631db00cadaf07ccb32b5fb51c5bdb51f39.jpg[/img]

[b]Statistical Details: [/b]For those requiring nuanced analytical data regarding every single Attachment, you can toggle “Details” on and off, which enables you to see how each attachment affects the weapon specifically, and numerically.

[b][u]Attachments: A Deep Dive[/u][/b]

The following showcases a variety of visuals for each Attachment type, along with notes on which weapons you can affix them to. The statistical benefits (and drawbacks as appropriate) are discussed, along with any further pertinent notes.

[b]Note: [/b]Any listing of a weapon type with an asterisk next to it (*) that you see indicates that some (but not all) of a weapon type use this Attachment.

[b]Optic[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/16fa19466cd3e556f5759efcf551328635f8ea6e.jpg[/img]

[b]Available on: [/b]Assault Rifles, SMGs, Shotguns, LMGs, Marksman Rifles, Sniper Rifles, Pistols.

[b]Not Available on: [/b]Launchers, Melee Weapons.

[b]Stat Benefit: [/b]Accuracy

Sights or scopes attached to the top of a weapon, designed to improve accuracy during target engagement. Occasionally improves Recoil Gun Kick. More powerful scopes (usually designed for Sniper Rifles) may reduce ADS Speed.

[b]Note:[/b] Optics are a unique type of Attachment as they are universal. This means that once you unlock an Optic, it becomes available for every weapon in the same class, not just the one you unlocked it for.

[b]Note:[/b] Optics come with Reticles; markings and dots that further delineate your targets and aid in your aiming. Your Optics can be further customized by unlocking a variety of Reticles via Reticle Challenges.

[b]Muzzle[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/850b331f1fee1aa7480e54304255332771bfd809.jpg[/img]

[b]Available on: [/b]Assault Rifles*, SMGs, Shotguns, LMGs, Marksman Rifles, Sniper Rifles, Pistols.

[b]Not Available on: [/b]Launchers, Melee Weapons.

[b]Stat Benefit: [/b]Accuracy

Usually attached to the end of the weapon barrel, Muzzles are used to redirect gasses (as necessary) and serve to reduce or control recoil.

[b]Barrel[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/e3b3aa4598317b390e2d53e98a7837ec16c0e07e.jpg[/img]

[b]Available on: [/b]Assault Rifles, SMGs, Shotguns, LMGs, Marksman Rifles, Sniper Rifles, Pistols.

[b]Not Available on: [/b]Launchers, Melee Weapons.

[b]Stat Benefit: [/b]Firepower

The front section of the weapon where the projectile travels through once the trigger has been pulled. Attachments tend to improve damage range and velocity, enabling you to hit a target more rapidly.

[b]Underbarrel[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/e81f1e86391b412d600b3284960d626f57cf8118.jpg[/img]

[b]Available on: [/b]Assault Rifles, SMGs*, Shotguns, LMGs, Marksman Rifles.

[b]Not Available on:[/b] Sniper Rifles, Pistols, Launchers, Melee Weapons.

[b]Stat Benefit: [/b]Firepower, Accuracy

Attached to the base of the barrel, Underbarrels come in two main varieties: Foregrips and Launchers. Foregrips are handles that can reduce recoil and sway (Accuracy). Launchers increase your firepower by adding an alt-fire capacity to the weapon, usually an explosive charge or grenade.

[b]Magazine[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/4da8eb44e56e8027fc01888b391c9c983072c3f9.jpg[/img]

[b]Available on: [/b]Assault Rifles, SMGs, Shotguns*, LMGs, Marksman Rifles, Sniper Rifles, Pistols.

[b]Not Available on: [/b]Launchers, Melee Weapons.

[b]Stat Benefit: [/b]Firepower or Handling

Magazines hold a weapon’s ammunition and are generally available in two types: Extended Mags allow you to carry more rounds, increasing Firepower sometimes at the expense of Handling. Fast or Flip Mags reduce your Firepower as you have fewer bullets but improve your Handling.

[b]Comb[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/5c943e440cafe4ca8208607ef0e8e91e420f97b9.jpg[/img]

[b]Available on: [/b]Sniper Rifles

[b]Not Available on: [/b]Assault Rifles, SMGs, Shotguns*, LMGs, Marksman Rifles, Pistols, Launchers, Melee Weapons.

[b]Stat Benefit: [/b]Handling

Also known as a Cheek Riser, Combs are Sniper Rifle-only head rests attached to the top of the Stock, and offer improved Handling, mainly decreasing the time it takes you to fire or ADS. This can come at the expense of Accuracy, depending on the specific Comb.

[b]Rear Grip[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/61435dcb99e513902837c30d21eafbab47495024.jpg[/img]

[b]Available on: [/b]Assault Rifles, SMGs, Shotguns*, LMGs, Marksman Rifles, Pistols.

[b]Not Available on: [/b]Sniper Rifles, Launchers, Melee Weapons.

[b]Stat Benefit: [/b]Handling

A rubber handle behind the weapon trigger. Attachments offer a variety of Handling improvements, usually decreasing the time it takes you to ADS, or fire under specific circumstances.

[b]Stock[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/498d90a7f31218673d0291968f9007b215ae1abc.jpg[/img]

[b]Available on: [/b]Assault Rifles, SMGs, Shotguns, LMGs, Marksman Rifles, Sniper Rifles, Pistols.

[b]Not Available on: [/b]Launchers, Melee Weapons.

[b]Stat Benefit: [/b]Accuracy or Mobility

These are braces enabling the Operator to support the armament against their shoulder and attach to the rear of the weapon. Generally, the lighter the stock Attachment, the more focused on increasing your Mobility (usually movement speed). Heavier stocks offer more benefits to your Accuracy (usually flinch resistance).

[b]Laser[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/ec037f07f111ff66246361608c58a787e705dd4b.jpg[/img]

[b]Available on: [/b]Assault Rifles, SMGs, Shotguns, LMGs, Marksman Rifles, Sniper Rifles, Pistols.

[b]Not Available on: [/b]Launchers, Melee Weapons.

[b]Stat Benefit: [/b]Accuracy

These side-mounted lasers (or under-mounted for Pistols) emit a beam of usually red or green light usually visible to the enemy. However, your Accuracy is significantly improved or augmented.

[b]NOTE:[/b] The Tactical Laser enables Tactical Stance, allowing you to balance your mobility and accuracy. This is the method to utilize the [i]Modern Warfare® III [/i]firing technique in [i]Black Ops 6[/i].

[b]Fire Mods[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/1369f47d57b849c288b15206091d1639f49dd3ba.jpg[/img]

[b]Available on: [/b]Assault Rifles, SMGs, Shotguns, LMGs, Marksman Rifles, Sniper Rifles, Pistols.

[b]Not Available on: [/b]Launchers, Melee Weapons.

[b]Stat Benefit: [/b]Firepower, Accuracy, or Handling (Varies depending on Fire Mod)

A “catch-all” of other Attachments, Fire Modifications have a variety of uses and are mainly focused into two subsets; improvements to parts of a weapon (examples include rapid fire triggers, pump guide rods, and recoil springs) and specific ammunition types (examples include FMJ or Overpressured rounds).

[b]Stock Pad[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/507b4cc4e27adc4b343939777fd6faa43c59bfd1.jpg[/img]

[b]Available on: [/b]Sniper Rifles*

[b]Not Available on: [/b]Assault Rifles, SMGs, Shotguns*, LMGs, Marksman Rifles, Pistols, Launchers, Melee Weapons.

[b]Stat Benefit: [/b]Accuracy

This Buttstock Pad Attachment is only available for the LW3A1 Frostline Sniper Rifle. Fitting into the shoulder of the Operator, the Stock Pads available improve Accuracy in discernable ways (improving Speed, Sway, or Recoil).

notes.title: Gear up: Equipment, perks, and Scorestreaks confirmed
notes.notes:
[b][u]Gear Up: Confirmation on Your Loadouts (MP, RBZ)[/u][/b]

[b]Recap: [/b]Perfecting your Loadouts in [i]Black Ops 6[/i] is both quick and easy. This includes a reworking of the Weapon Gunsmith to make it much more approachable, allowing you to choose from the vast array of unlockable weapon attachments with a renewed set of confidence that the build you’re making is suited to your exact style of play.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/1a767a84e5b829521b9ea2541731720201cc875d.jpg[/img]

It all starts in the Weapons Menu, and it’s here you’ll choose your Loadouts. [i]Black Ops 6[/i] is set to bring an exceptional arsenal of weaponry and equipment to the game – including 12 weapons all-new to the franchise – and the following information details the available Equipment (Tacticals, Lethals, Field Upgrades) Scorestreaks, Perks, Combat Specialties, and Wildcards available at the game’s launch.

[b]Weapons Detail Note: [/b]The Primary, Secondary, and Melee Weapons you can choose from, along with Gunsmith and Attachment Intel, is covered in the Weapons Detail Blog, available here.

[b]Zombies Detail Note: [/b]Round-Based Zombies Mode utilizes some (but not all) of the Equipment detailed in this blog. Where appropriate, this will be flagged. Expect a Launch Comms: Zombies-focused blog prior to game release that confirms all Equipment available at launch for this mode.

[b]Mastery Badges Note: [/b]Every Equipment set – Tacticals, Lethals, Field Upgrades, and Scorestreaks – have their own Medal Challenge (with associated XP Reward), and all individual Equipment items have a specific set of Mastery Badge Challenges to complete. Consult the Launch Comms: Progression Blog for more Intel.

[b]Accessing Loadouts[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/06f1fe8622a9fd24fe5096d0236f2f3016f4f3b5.jpg[/img]

Loadouts are the key to accessing all the wealth of Operator equipment in the game. At the very start of your [i]Black Ops 6[/i] Multiplayer journey, you’re able to access Default Loadouts (that are pre-built for a specific style of play), but the entire Loadout content opens once you hit Player Level 4, and Custom Loadouts become available, as shown below:

[b]Progression: Loadout Unlocks[/b]

Loadout - Player Level

ENFORCER 1

RECON 1

STRATEGIST 1

COMMANDO 2

OVERWATCH 3

CUSTOM 4

[b][u]Overview: Tacticals (8) (MP, RBZ)[/u][/b]

[b][i]Mastery Badges available for this Equipment Type[/i][/b]

[b]Recap: [/b]Tacticals are limited-per-life and reusable items that range from intel-gathering sensors to healing or disorientation devices, designed to offer a non-lethal advantage in combat.

[b]Wildcard Note: [/b]Equip the Tactical Expert Wildcard, and you spawn with two additional Tacticals of the same type (a total of three).

[b]Progression: Tacticals Unlocks[/b]

Tactical - Player Level

CONCUSSION 0

FLASHBANG 6

SPY CAM 12

SMOKE 17

PROX ALARM 23

STIM SHOT 30

DECOY 35

SHOCK CHARGE 42

[b]Available Tacticals[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/5183795136410bfc164b6a7ac6ca77b0f102e485.jpg[/img]

[b]Concussion Grenade (MP, RBZ)[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked Immediately

Grenade that slows victim’s movement and aiming.

[b]Flashbang Grenade (MP)[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked at Player Level 6

Grenade that blinds targets for a duration. For players with photosensitivity concerns, the flash effect of this grenade can be displayed as a low-light black effect if you change it at the Options > Graphics > View > Inverted Flashbang menu.

[b]Spy Cam (MP)[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked at Player Level 12

Quickly mark enemies and hostile Equipment and Scorestreaks for your team.

[b]Smoke Grenade (MP, RBZ)[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked at Player Level 17

Deploys a smoke screen that blocks vision and automated targeting systems.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/7e7e30b2415f10d7bc9788cae25546f4c7808c1e.jpg[/img]

[b]Prox Alarm (MP)[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked at Player Level 23

Set of two sticky alarms that ring and flash when an enemy is nearby. Tripped alarms show on allied minimaps.

[b]Stim Shot (MP, RBZ)[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked at Player Level 30

Combat stim that heals wounds and refreshes Tactical Sprint.

[b]Decoy Grenade (MP, RBZ)[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked at Player Level 35

Grenade that simulates footsteps and gunfire sounds to confuse enemies. Sticks to surfaces.

[b]Shock Charge (MP, RBZ)[/b]

[b]Available:[/b] Unlocked at Player Level 42

Electrical trap that sticks to surfaces and electrocutes enemies, stunning them.

[b][u]Overview: Lethals (9) (MP, RBZ)[/u][/b]

[b][i]Mastery Badges available for this Equipment Type[/i][/b]

[b]Recap: [/b]Lethals are limited-per-life items that harm enemies, usually via an explosion.

[b]Wildcard Note: [/b]Equip the Danger Close Wildcard, and you spawn with two additional Lethals of the same type (a total of three).

[b]Progression: Lethals Unlocks[/b]

Lethal Player Level

FRAG 0

STICKY GRENADE 9

C4 14

THERMO GRENADE 21

IMPACT GRENADE 26

MOLOTOV 32

BLAST TRAP 41

DRILL CHARGE 50

[b]Combat Specialty:[/b] In addition to the name and combat capabilities, each [i]Black Ops 6[/i] Perk has color associated with it. This visual reference denotes the Combat Specialty the Perk offers, but only if grouped with two other Perks of the same color (or Specialty).
[list]	[*]The three colors are Red (Enforcer), Blue (Recon), and Green (Strategist).[/*]	[*]For example, “Engineer” (Perk 2) is color-coded blue, meaning it grants the Recon Combat Specialty, but only if your two other Perks (from Perk selections 1 and 3) are also color-coded blue (i.e., they are also grant the “Recon” Specialty).[/*]	[*]Choose three Perks of the same color in slots 1, 2, and 3, and you’re able to pick an additional Specialty.[/*][/list]

notes.title: RICOCHET Anti-Cheat™ Progress Report: Black Ops 6 launch
notes.notes:
On October 25, [i]Call of Duty®: Black Ops[/i] 6 launches and RICOCHET Anti-Cheat will be live on Day One, bringing with it new technology and upgrades to protect your experience.

When it first launched, RICOCHET Anti-Cheat committed to providing players with clear and transparent communication on our methods to protect the Call of Duty community from cheaters. Our technology and methods of detection have evolved so much, but the “how” and “when” we talk to the community simply needs to be more frequent and in line with our evolution.

The RICOCHET Anti-Cheat team has heard your feedback, and this progress report was written to provide a meaningful update on the issue of cheating as well as outline the foundation for the year to come beginning with the launch of [i]Black Ops 6[/i] and what lies beyond.

Over the last year, we have been investing in numerous core systems focused on decreasing the time gap between when cheating occurs and when our systems are able to act. By building on this foundation, we will be able to evolve more quickly and respond more rapidly (more on how fast we are trying to be later).

[b][i]What Does #TeamRICOCHET Do?[/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/58a0f8152345cb9dba92a879aa3a4fe8109d96b4.jpg[/img]

We protect [i]Call of Duty[/i] games. We often achieve that goal but know there is so much more work to do. So, what is cheating in [i]Call of Duty[/i]? Simply put, it is anything that gives a player an unfair advantage in-game using nefarious software, like wall hacks or perfect aim – not to be confused with any abuse of in-game glitches. Cheating also includes account sharing to unlock gear, using software to get access to items you haven’t earned or purchased, and account boosting.

All of these actions are against our [url=https://support.activision.com/articles/call-of-duty-security-and-enforcement-policy]Security and Enforcement Policy[/url].

And you might be wondering, how do people cheat in online games? Put simply, cheaters use software to manipulate the game, to reveal information that shouldn’t be known, or to take automated actions with superhuman speed or accuracy. We all know cars shouldn’t fly in this slice of the multiverse, but sometimes our in-game worlds [i]disagree[/i].

The people behind cheats are organized, illegal groups that pick apart every piece of data within our games to look for some way to make cheating possible. These bad guys are not just some script kiddies poking around with code they found online. They are a collective who profit from exploiting the hard work of game developers across the industry.

But cheat developers are flawed (clearly – they have to pretend to be good at video games). Every time they cheat, they leave breadcrumbs behind. There are several ways we find those breadcrumbs, for example:
[list]	[*]#TeamRICOCHET’s kernel-level driver for PC that runs as you play the game[/*]	[*]Server-side and client-side detections[/*]	[*]Machine learning models that look for anomalies and examine matches[/*]	[*]Anti-Cheat’s Replay Investigation Tool[/*]	[*]Third-party hardware detections and more[/*][/list]

[b][i]How Are We Protecting [/i][/b][b]Black Ops 6[i]?[/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/10468df12fb27e92604039404cfab4e15b4e3534.jpg[/img]

The number one thing both we and you care about is not losing another match to a cheater. A lot has been put into [i]Black Ops 6[/i] to upgrade security, but here is the goal we’re targeting: [b]we want to catch and remove cheaters within one hour of them being in their first match.[/b]

This metric is called “[i]Time to Action[/i],” and we will be monitoring our progress internally and building technology to drive this number down.

During the [i]Black Ops 6[/i] Beta, our team was live testing a lot of its new tech to try and achieve this goal. Weekend One was a stumble. In the past, we’ve used data from console players during Beta Weekend One to train and test our systems. Put simply, even though we love our friends who game on PC, it’s nice to have a weekend to stress test systems without the risk of cheaters. Since we had to protect the game without those stress tests, our new technology was so eager to catch cheaters, that it came in a little hot. When we recognized those errors, we immediately made adjustments to correct course in service of our new [i]Time to Action[/i] milestone.

Cheaters were able to complete around 10 multiplayer matches during Weekend One before being removed. After tweaking our systems and deploying new detection methods for Weekend Two, we cut that time in half to 5 matches. That timing achieved our Time to Action goal. In fact, 25% of all Weekend Two bans happened during the first match a cheater ever played.

But removing someone after they cheat isn’t perfect, so we are ramping up detections to try to stop even more cheaters before they load into a game. During the beta we stopped over 12,000 confirmed cheating accounts before they ever saw the inside of a match.

[i]Black Ops 6[/i] on Day One is going to launch with a variety of updated anti-cheat tech. To name a few:
[list]	[*]An updated version of the kernel-level driver. Note: All features in the October 25 update will protect any title that uses the driver, including [i]Call of Duty®: Warzone™.[/i][/*]	[*]All mitigations, including Damage Shield, Disarm, Splat, Hallucination, and others will be live.[/*]	[*]New machine-learning behavioral systems, focused on speed of detection.[/*]	[*]New machine-learning detection models to analyze gameplay to combat aim bots.[/*]	[*]Upgrades when Ranked Play launches, which include continuous examinations to determine if leaderboard placements are accurate. More on Ranked Play updates in a future blog closer the mode’s launch.[/*]	[*]For [i]Call of Duty: Warzone[/i] specifically, we’ve deployed new mitigations to interrupt cheaters. Stay tuned for a future report to learn about those new tricks.[/*][/list]
We’re always looking for those breadcrumbs to find the bad actors and get them out of the game. That’s our commitment to the community.


[b][i]What’s Ahead[/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/152069425bb1d335fb4a7c853d9da9cee2648de3.jpg[/img]

While #TeamRICOCHET continues to develop and deploy client and server-side anti-cheat systems, we’re looking at what comes next. Fighting cheats today – on the client where illicit programs are activated – is a little like battling on a bad guy’s home turf: it is their machine and their code.

Kernel-Level Drivers on PC have enhanced anti-cheat’s reach, but cheaters are already offering cheats that go beyond the kernel, even going as far to utilize special PC hardware that is designed entirely for attacking games and enabling cheating.

What our team has been working on for the future is a suite of tools that use AI to find and fight cheaters.

Today, cheaters can run and hide but a trail exists. What if that trail disappears? That is what the team has been working on. Cheat developers can’t hide player behavior. How people play – the legit, the phony, the good, and the bad – gives us information and we use that to build ways to pick those bad folks out of a lineup.

We already have data from cheaters but to help build out profiles for those God-tier players we examine the data from the [i]Call of Duty League [/i]– where every match is recorded, and every stat is preserved.

There’s more in progress around what we’re doing with AI beyond behavioral models and as work continues, we’ll share what we can.

[b][i]Our Commitment[/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/37829e41b48591d1b4926eb4cfff43d63fc1c451.jpg[/img]

Cheating is a frustrating issue across the industry. But our goal is to get bad actors out of our game as fast as possible. Our NorthStar is within one hour.

We’ve had a lot of wins over the years – taking down several cheat developers completely, shutting out third-party hardware, flinging cheaters toward the ground at Mach-speed – but we know those wins don’t make you feel any better when you get beamed by a cheater from across the map.

We can’t tell you cheaters will disappear forever because of the tech we’re preparing for launch. But everyone at #TeamRICOCHET will use every tool we can to keep fighting to deliver a fair and fun experience for you! And if the right tool doesn’t exist, we’ll make it ourselves. Anti-cheat is a constant effort, and we are always working to stop and thwart the efforts of cheaters. It’s an effort we’re deeply committed to, through and through.

Keep an eye out for updates in future Progress Reports and across social media, particularly the @CODUpdates X (formerly known as Twitter) social account for real-time issues.

[i]For more information on Activision games, follow @Activision on X (formerly Twitter), Facebook, and Instagram.[/i]
