Unlock Criteria:

            Complete the Platinum Camo challenge for the specific weapon (MP Mastery).

            Complete a total of 51 Platinum Camo challenges for MWII weapons (MP Mastery).

            Complete the Arachnida Camo Challenge: Usually a set number of Special or Elite Zombie Kills with the weapon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/6a22680684f95806fe167c28c6e3a6697e4dab2c.jpg[/img]

[b]Bioluminescent[/b] (animated, available for [i]MWII[/i] weapons only).

            Complete a total of 32 Arachnida Camo challenges for MWII weapons.

[b]Weapon Mastery Unlock Criteria: [/b]

[b]Golden Ivory Emblem and Calling Card:[/b] Unlock Golden Ivory Camo, get 300 Kills while using the Golden Ivory Camo in Zombies.

[b]Spinel Husk Emblem and Calling Card:[/b] Complete Golden Ivory Mastery, Unlock Spinel Husk Camo, get 600 Kills while using the Spinel Husk Camo in Zombies.

[b]Arachnida Emblem and Calling Card:[/b] Complete Spinel Husk Mastery, Unlock Arachnida Camo, get 900 Kills while using the Arachnida Camo in Zombies.

[b]NEW: [i]MWIII[/i] Completionist Camos (MWZ Mastery)[/b]

            Complete all four Zombie Base Camo Challenges for the specific weapon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/3b94272dde185e39716ba78bc348966bc52c5277.jpg[/img]

Unlock Criteria:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/18adfa94d064a7ee7e899287911cd05634a364aa.jpg[/img]

[b]Serpentinite[/b] (animated, available for [i]MWIII[/i] weapons only).

Unlock Criteria:

            Complete the Zircon Scale Camo challenge for the specific weapon.

            Complete a total of 37 Zircon Scale Camo challenges for MWIII weapons.

            Complete the Serpentinite Camo Challenge: Usually a set number of Special or Elite Zombie Kills with the weapon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/c16fc33baea577dc51ee92cfea13225e4771a51b.jpg[/img]

[b]Borealis[/b] (animated, available for [i]MWIII[/i] weapons only).

Unlock Criteria:

            Complete a total of 37 Serpentinite Camo challenges for MWIII weapons.

[b]Weapon Mastery Unlock Criteria: [/b]

[b]Golden Enigma Emblem and Calling Card:[/b] Unlock Golden Enigma Camo, get 300 Kills while using the Golden Enigma Camo in Zombies.

[b]Zicron Scale Emblem and Calling Card:[/b] Complete Golden Enigma Mastery, Unlock Zicron Scale Camo, get 600 Kills while using the Zicron Scale Camo in Zombies.

[b]Serpentinite Emblem and Calling Card:[/b] Complete Zicron Scale Mastery, Unlock Serpentinite Camo, get 900 Kills while using the Serpentinite Camo in Zombies.

[b]Borealis Emblem and Calling Card:[/b] Complete Serpentinite Mastery, Unlock Borealis Camo, get 1,200 Kills while using the Borealis Camo in Zombies.

[b]Completionist Charm: [/b]Complete all Mastery Challenges.

[b][i]Modern Warfare III: Weapon Camo Synopsis[/i][/b]

Information overload? Then read on as we conclude this blog with a reasonably concise summary:

The [i]Modern Warfare III[/i] Weapon Camo system is familiar but comes with additional innovations and a vastly larger pool of camos to unlock. As in [i]MWII[/i], camos are split into two groups: Base and Completionist (Mastery):

[b]New Base Camos ([i]MWIII[/i] MP, MWZ)[/b]
[list]	[*]There are 18 brand new Base Camo sets in [i]MWIII[/i].[/*]	[*]New Base Camos are unlocked by completing Challenges using [i]MWIII[/i] weaponry.[/*]	[*]New Base Camos are unlocked in both Multiplayer and Zombies.[/*]	[*]Multiplayer: Expect four Base Camos per [i]MWIII[/i] Primary Weapon and Handgun.[/*]	[*]Zombies: Expect four Base Camos per [i]MWIII[/i] Primary Weapon and Handgun.[/*]	[*]Expect one Base Camo per [i]MWIII[/i] Launcher and Melee for MP, and the same for Zombies.[/*][/list]

notes.title: Gear Up: Modern Warfare III Loadouts: What You Need to Know
notes.notes:
Prior to a match, the Weapons menu of [i]Modern Warfare III [/i]allows you to select, edit, and save up to 10 Customized Loadouts for Multiplayer: selections of armaments and equipment. This is generally the same as the legacy term “Create-a-Class.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/439bb6e362af950b1d072b79943584dfceef8d4b.jpg[/img]

[b]Note: [/b]The process is different for Multiplayer and Zombies. While Zombies has access to your available weapon arsenal, other equipment is accessed differently, and there’s an impressive amount of Zombies-only ordnance to utilize and unlock. Perks, Field Upgrades, and some Killstreaks will not be available in MWZ. Consult the Modern Warfare Zombies Overview Blog, prior to game launch.

[b]Note: [/b]The following equipment is scheduled to be available at game launch. Additional equipment of various types may appear after launch.
[b]Loadout Overview: Multiplayer (and Zombies)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/39f3a4d094d6f5f44632f0914942dd6ab485bd61.jpg[/img]

Each Loadout is presented in a familiar layout, but with one important difference: the type of Vest you choose governs the number of Equipment pieces you can carry and offers you a particular set of Perk-like skills.

[b]Note[/b]: Loadouts are unlocked at Player Level 4. Modern Warfare Zombies uses a different Perk and Field Upgrade system, but does employ a selection of Tacticals and Lethals that are shared with Multiplayer.

[b][i]Gear Up: The Evolution of Perks (MP only)[/i][/b]

[b]Vests, Gloves, Boots, and Gear [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/231bedaba9ac31013b2e24010d272dd82aa9ee26.jpg[/img]

When choosing a Vest, it is important to know that same Vests remove (or increase) the number of Tacticals, Lethals, Field Upgrades, Gloves, Boots, and Gear you can carry into matches. Therefore, it’s worthwhile picking a Vest first.

[b]Tip: [/b]The key to an effective Loadout is to pick Vests, Gloves, Boots, and Gear with complementary abilities, which further augment your Primary and Secondary Weapon, as well as the Tactical, Lethal, and Field Upgrade Equipment you are carrying.

[b]Vests (6, MP only)[/b]

The following Vests are available at the launch of [i]Modern Warfare III[/i]:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/2f7b1a91522b95d57702743ae17ed68efa43f570.jpg[/img]

[b]Infantry Vest[/b]

Equipment Slots (3): Tactical, Lethal, Field Upgrade

Gear Slots (3): Gloves, Boots, Gear

[i]Standard issue mobile infantry vest. Increases Tac Sprint duration and reduces refresh time. Duplicate effects do not stack. If equipped with Running Sneakers (Boots), you gain the effects of Lightweight Boots (Boots).[/i]

[b]Engineer Vest[/b]

Equipment Slots (3): Tactical x2, Field Upgrade (Lethal Slot removed)

Gear Slots (4): Gloves, Boots, Gear x2

[i]Counter equipment and explosives expertise. Spot enemy equipment, Field Upgrades, and Killstreaks through walls. Aiming down sights highlights them for the team. Faster Field Upgrade recharge.[/i]

[b]Gunner Vest[/b]

Equipment Slots (3): Two Primary Weapons, Tactical, Lethal, Field Upgrade (Secondary Weapon Slot removed)

Gear Slots (2): Gloves, Gear (Boots Slot removed)

[i]Weapon and ammo focused kit. Deploy with max ammo. Improved reload speed. Duplicate effects do not stack. If equipped with Mag Holster (Gear), gain the effects of Mission Control Commlink (Gear).[/i]

[b]Demolition Vest[/b]

Equipment Slots (4): Tactical, Lethal x2, Field Upgrade

Gear Slots (3): Gloves, Boots, Gear

[i]Lethal and Tactical mastery. Resupply Lethal and Tactical Equipment every 25 seconds.[/i]

[b]CCT Comms Vest[/b]

Equipment Slots (1): Field Upgrade (Tactical and Lethal Slots removed)

Gear Slots: (4)L Gloves, Boots, Gear x2

[i]Team intelligence resource. Increases duration enemies stay on radar and zooms out radar for you and nearby allies. Enemies you kill drop intel packs, which generate a radar ping for you and nearby allies when collected. Duplicate effects do not stack. If equipped with Data Jacker (Gear), gain the effects of Mission Control Commlink (Gear).[/i]

[b]Overkill[/b][b] Vest[/b]

Equipment Slots (2): Tactical, Lethal (Field Upgrade Slot removed)

Gear Slots (3): Gloves, Boots, Gear

[i]Mastery of weapon mobility. Increased weapon swap speed. Reload while sprinting. Duplicate effects do not stack. If equipped with Quick-Grip Gloves (Gloves), or Commando Gloves (Gloves), gain the effects of Marksman Gloves (Gloves).[/i]

[b]Gloves (6, MP only)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/2dc3be6f3f63f2afc7afd1033b549ae3b43820d2.jpg[/img]

Gloves have Perks that specifically improve the handling of your Primary and Secondary Weapons, as well influence your interactions with Tactical and Lethal Equipment. Every Vest allows you to pick one pair of Gloves from the following:

[b]Quick-Grip Gloves[/b]

[i]Increased weapon swap speed.[/i]

[b]Ordnance Gloves[/b]

[i]Throw equipment farther. Reset fuse timer on thrown back grenades.[/i]

[b]Commando Gloves[/b]

[i]Reload while sprinting.[/i]

[b]Scavenger Gloves[/b]

[i]Resupply ammo and throwing knives from dead players.[/i]

[b]Marksman Gloves[/b]

[i]Reduced sway and flinch while ADS.[/i]

[b]Assault Gloves[/b]

[i]While jumping, accuracy and time to ADS is improved.[/i]

[b]Boots (6, MP only)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/c559c429783ee6c3f1265ebc98dbe06114ae9d7d.jpg[/img]

Boots have Perks that specifically improve your movement and swimming, as well as how loud and maneuverable you are. Every Vest (except the Gunner Vest) allows you to pick one pair of Boots from the following:

[b]Lightweight Boots[/b]

[i]Increases movement and swim speed. Reduces noise while swimming.[/i]

[b]Climbing Boots[/b]

[i]Increased climbing and mantling speed. Reduces fall damage.[/i]

[b]Running Sneakers[/b]

[i]Increases Tac Sprint duration and reduces refresh time.[/i]

[b]Tactical Pads[/b]

[i]Increases slide distance and allows for aiming down sights while sliding. Increases stance transition speeds and crouched movement speed.[/i]

[b]Stalker Boots[/b]

[i]Increased strafe and ADS movement speed.[/i]

[b]Covert Sneakers[/b]

[i]Eliminates footstep sounds.[/i]

[b]Gear (12, MP only)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/b5fb257ffbf9bf07a062e16c681a898198e2e67f.jpg[/img]

Gear has Perks that have a wide-ranging selection of improvements to a variety of skill sets, related to weapon handling, immunities, early warning systems, and damage reduction. Every Vest allows you to run one of the following pieces of Gear, and the Engineer and CCT Comms Vests allow two:

[b]Tac Mask[/b]

[i]Reduces strength of enemy flash, stun, and gas grenades. [/i]

[b]Mission Control Commlink[/b]

[i]Reduce Killstreak cost by one (1) kill. Reduce Scorestreak cost by 125.[/i]

[b]Bone Conduction Headset[/b]

[i]Reduces combat noise, allowing improved identification of enemy footsteps and gunshots.[/i]

[b]Mag Holster[/b]

[i]Improved reload speed.[/i]

[b]Blacklight Flashlight[/b]

[i]Shows recent enemy footsteps.[/i]

[b]L/R Detector[/b]

[i]Warns of hostile laser and radiation sources.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/6b2c362937aa1e867a1d877f790b7e425963ca14.jpg[/img]

[b]Threat Identification System[/b]

[i]While ADS, automatically pings enemy locations in crosshairs.[/i]

[b]Data Jacker[/b]

[i]Enemies you kill drop a smartphone. Collecting the smartphone generates a radar ping from that location.[/i]

[b]Signal Jammer[/b]

[i]Emits a signal disrupting placed enemy claymores and mines. Warns of nearby enemy equipment.[/i]

[b]Hijacked IFF Strobe[/b]

[i]Undetectable by AI targeting systems and thermal optics. Does not highlight in enemy Tactical Cameras or Recon Drones.[/i]

[b]Ghost T/V Camo[/b]

[i]While moving, blocks detection by UAVs, enemy radar sources, and Heartbeat Sensors.[/i]

[b]EOD Padding[/b]

[i]Reduces damage from non-killstreak explosives and fire.[/i]

[b]Equipment Overview: Tacticals and Lethals (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[b]Tacticals (12, MP, MWZ)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/618f63bca1375b4bcc96c0af238b4d2b42faab92.jpg[/img]

A complement of 12 pieces of Tactical Equipment is available for every Operator, 11 in Multiplayer and 7 in Zombies. Add to your Loadout (in Multiplayer, you can carry none, one, or two, depending on the Vest you’ve equipped) from the following:

[b]Stun Grenade (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Slows victim’s movement and aiming.[/i]

[b]Battle Rage (MP)[/b]

[i]Experimental stimulant that gives you an adrenaline rush. Health regenerates quickly, Tactical Equipment is resisted, and Tactical Sprint is constantly refreshed.[/i]

[b]Smoke Grenade (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Deploys a smoke screen that blocks vision and automated targeting systems.[/i]

[b]Scatter[/b][b] Mine (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Throw a field of mines across a wide area that detonates when enemies come within range.[/i]

[b]Decoy Grenade (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Counter-intel grenade that simulates gunfire, movement, and radar signatures to confuse the enemy.[/i]

[b]Flash Grenade (MP)[/b]

[i]Blinds and deafens targets.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/6626d13d219f017abf48776f340a6109d2888c6b.jpg[/img]

[b]Snapshot Grenade (MP)[/b]

[i]Provides a momentary glimpse of enemies within the blast radius for your team or squad.[/i]

[b]Shock Stick (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Electrical device that sticks to surfaces. Electrocutes enemies, destroys equipment, and causes vehicles to go haywire.[/i]

[b]Stim (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Military stimulant that promotes clotting to close wounds quickly and refreshes Tactical Sprint.[/i]

[b]Tear Gas (MP)[/b]

[i]Explodes on impact with the ground, releasing a lingering cloud of tear gas that causes slowed movement, blurred vision, and coughing.[/i]

[b]Experimental Gas Grenade (MWZ)[/b]

[i]Grenade that releases a lingering cloud of gas that causes slowed movement, blurred vision, coughing, and light damage.[/i]

[b]EMD Grenade (MP)[/b]

[i]Applies a tracking device to enemies hit, revealing them on your team’s minimap.[/i]

[b]Lethals (12, MP, MWZ)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/7780727f00e610aba07bc6fad85312f10d9d4046.jpg[/img]

A total of 12 pieces of Lethal Equipment is available for every Operator, 11 in Multiplayer and 10 in Zombies. Add to your Loadout (in Multiplayer, you can carry none, one, or two, depending on the Vest you’ve equipped) from the following:

[b]Frag Grenade (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Cookable fragmentation grenade.[/i]

[b]Claymore (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Proximity-activated explosive mine.[/i]

[b]Throwing Knife (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Retrievable throwing knife that is lethal on impact in Core MP.[/i]

[b]Thermite (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Explosive incendiary device that sticks to all surfaces.[/i]

[b]Thermobaric Grenade (MP)[/b]

[i]Cookable grenade. Creates a large explosion that stuns, leaves a fiery residue, and increases the lethality of explosives for a period of time.[/i]

[b]Proximity Mine (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Proximity-triggered explosive that launches in the air, and deals heavy damage to the surrounding area.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/60ab200fe35de99b01ff517a2a39188e5ab70bb1.jpg[/img]

[b]Drill Charge (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Charge with a thermal lance that can burrow into surfaces before exploding.[/i]

[b]Semtex (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Timed sticky grenade.[/i]

[b]C4 (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Large explosive that sticks to surfaces and can be detonated remotely using a “use Lethal Equipment” button when the equipment is deployed. Double-tapping the “Interact/Reload” button always detonates the explosives.[/i]

[b]Molotov Cocktail (MWZ)[/b]

[i]Improvised incendiary device that explodes on impact.[/i]

[b]Throwing Star (MP)[/b]

[i]A swift and deadly throwing star that inflicts a wounding effect on the target.[/i]

[b]Breacher Drone (MP, MWZ)[/b]

[i]Explosive drone that explodes on proximity to an enemy or on impact.[/i]

[b]Equipment Overview: Field Upgrades (18, [/b][b]MP only)[/b]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/43f8188ee14ba4f8d0c6a8945a4a6b759813cf5a.jpg[/img]

Additional equipment utilized after a recharge period, Field Upgrades are the final piece of the individual Loadout. Every Operator can carry one (or none, depending on the Vest equipped) from the following:

[b]Heartbeat Sensor[/b]

[i]A limited use tablet that displays rough information about nearby enemies.[/i]

[b]Med Box[/b]

[i]Deploy a box of medical supplies for you and your teammates to reduce healing delay.[/i]

[b]Inflatable Decoy[/b]

[i]Proximity activated decoy mine. Upon activation the reinforced fiber target is violently deployed to confuse and distract. Press the ‘Tactical and Lethal’ buttons together a second time for manual activation.[/i]

[b]Comm Scrambler[/b]

[i]Disables communication with intel within its radius. Enemies will not be able to activate killstreaks. Enemy UAV and intel systems will not detect you and your teammates. Location of the scrambler is visible in the enemy minimap.[/i]

[b]Tactical Insertion[/b]

[i]Marks a location as your next spawn point. Tactical Insertion doesn’t have an effect in one-life modes, such as Search & Destroy.[/i]

[b]Trophy System[/b]

[i]Deployable autonomous defense system that destroys up to three nearby pieces of equipment and projectiles. Some larger targets may take multiple shots.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/d6634c50f2eea9d44b2afe2901c20d04a5d65770.jpg[/img]

[b]Munitions Box[/b]

[i]Deploy a box of ammo and equipment for you and your teammates.[/i]

[b]A.C.S.[/b]

[i]An Automated Computer Spike slowly captures points and temporarily hacks nearby enemy devices. Point capturing applies in the following modes: Domination, Hardpoint, Control, Ground War.[/i]

[b]Tactical Camera[/b]

[i]Remote-controlled camera that marks enemies. Press the ‘Tactical and Lethal Buttons’ to throw it, and press again to connect to it. When left on its own, the camera will monitor the area and warn players of nearby enemies by sound.[/i]

[b]DDoS[/b]

[i]Activates a device that deactivates electronics, and disrupts enemy sensors in the immediate area for a short time.[/i]

[b]Deployable Cover[/b]

[i]Portable, rapidly deployable ballistic cover.[/i]

[b]Recon Drone[/b]

[i]Remote-controlled drone that has manual and auto marking capabilities.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/8f31a3930d9d3c1a2a2b00bab9aa46dfe2f7042b.jpg[/img]

[b]Dead Silence[/b]

[i]Temporarily makes your footsteps silent. Gun, melee, and throwing knife kills refresh duration.[/i]

[b]Loadout Drop[/b]

[i]Call in a team-based loadout crate with limited uses. Each player can only use it once.[/i]

[b]Portable Radar[/b]

[i]Emits a periodic radar ping to detect nearby enemies.[/i]

[b]Smoke Airdrop[/b]

[i]Call in a line of drones to deploy a smoke wall at a targeted location.[/i]

[b]Suppression Mine[/b]

[i]Trip mine that when triggered, emits a constant sound wave that disrupts enemy vision and slows their movement.[/i]

[b]Anti-Armor Rounds[/b]

[i]Gives weapon ammo that applies bonus damage against armored targets; this includes vehicles, equipment, body armor, and targets behind penetrable cover.[/i]

[b]Equipment Overview: Killstreaks and Scorestreaks (25, MP, MWZ)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/b9531bafa3857c048a333aa0d7fa60f5b27ac766.jpg[/img]

A full and impressive complement of mainly harder-hitting offensive (or reconnaissance) capabilities become available to your Operator as you level up through the Military Ranks. You can pick three Killstreaks, and choose whether they become available after a certain number of enemy kills (Killstreaks) or after you score a certain number of points by completing in-match actions (Scorestreaks).

Note that Modern Warfare Zombies utilizes Killstreaks in a different manner, and has a smaller pool of them to access.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/131d78f141b1dbc89ccf9dacf8c18b654dba1eb1.jpg[/img]

[b]UAV[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 4

Scorestreak Needed: 500

[i]UAV recon ship that reveals enemy locations on the minimap.[/i]

[b]NEW: Mosquito Drone[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 4

Scorestreak Needed: 500

[i]Explosive drone that circles the area around where the drone is launched. Dive bombs on enemies it spots and explodes.[/i]

[b]NEW: SAM Turret[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 4

Scorestreak Needed: 500

[i]Launch a targeted missile strike against air vehicles.[/i]

[b]Bomb Drone[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 4

Scorestreak Needed: 500

[i]A remote-controlled drone with an attached C4 charge.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/4c9a6f6a6ea391301b4c079d00b94a30c9b5916a.jpg[/img]

[b]NEW: Guardian-SC[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 5

Scorestreak Needed: 625

[i]A beam shaped, non-lethal, area denial weapon. Enemies entering the beam have similar effects to a stun grenade, reduced movement speed, blurred vision, and removed UI.[/i]

[b]Care Package[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 5

Scorestreak Needed: 625

[i]Call in a random killstreak care package to your location.[/i]

[b]Counter UAV[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 5

Scorestreak Needed: 625

[i]A drone that scrambles all enemy minimaps.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/61db9b9b0e2620a76a6c81e047681513b07fdd5e.jpg[/img]

[b]Cluster Mine[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 6

Scorestreak Needed: 750

[i]Throw a device that launches a cluster of smaller mines within the immediate area.[/i]

[b]Precision Airstrike[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 6

Scorestreak Needed: 750

[i]Call in twin jets for a precision strike along the best available path.[/i]

[b]Cruise Missile[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 6

Scorestreak Needed:750

[i]Control a long-range cruise missile with boost capabilities.[/i]

[b]NEW: Remote Turret[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 7

Scorestreak Needed: 875

[i]Automated turret that scans for nearby enemies and fires incendiary based rounds.[/i]

[b]Mortar Strike[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 7

Scorestreak Needed: 875

[i]Signal several waves of mortars to attack a location.[/i]

[b]SAE[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 7

Scorestreak Needed: 875

[i]Call in a trio of jets to release aerial explosives onto specified targets.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/3245eb663479242935b54352ff2ca7e0af26ef8f.jpg[/img]

[b]NEW: Juggernaut Recon[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 8

Scorestreak Needed: 1,000

[i]Juggernaut Recon gear delivered by care package. The suit is equipped with a radar that pings nearby enemies. Contains a riot shield, Haymaker and smoke grenade.[/i]

[b]Wheelson-HS[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 8

Scorestreak Needed: 1,000

[i]Remote controlled amphibious vehicle with auto sentry capabilities.[/i]

[b]Overwatch Helo[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 8

Scorestreak Needed: 1,000

[i]An escort helo that will watch over your position and ping nearby enemy locations before engaging them.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/c54cb8e9ad9fd73062ee8676c25760af011997c8.jpg[/img]

[b]VTOL Jet[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 10

Scorestreak Needed: 1,250

[i]Releases a pair of precision bombs before circling back and guarding a location of the player’s choice.[/i]

[b]Emergency Airdrop[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 10

Scorestreak Needed: 1,250

[i]Call in three random killstreak care packages to your location.[/i]

[b]Carpet Bomb[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 10

Scorestreak Needed: 1,250

[i]Call in a bomber that releases a large line of explosives along its path.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/0501a44f37e3d215f90b0f8f733c20f7ae45fbd3.jpg[/img]

[b]Advanced UAV[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 12

Scorestreak Needed: 1,500

[i]An untargetable orbital UAV that reveals the enemy’s direction on the minimap in real time.[/i]

[b]Chopper Gunner[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 12

Scorestreak Needed: 1,500

[i]Control an assault chopper armored with a turret and air-to-land missiles.[/i]

[b]Gunship[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 12

Scorestreak Needed: 1,500

[i]A heavy assault gunship equipped with a laser tracking missile, along with the standard 40mm and 25mm cannons.[/i]

[b]Juggernaut[/b]

Killstreak Needed: 15

Scorestreak Needed: 1,875

[i]Juggernaut assault gear delivered by care package. The minigun will drop when the Juggernaut dies.[/i]

[b][i]Modern Warfare III Launch Comms Continues[/i][/b]

Be sure to check back at the Call of Duty Blog between now and launch, as we confirm in-game content and offer deep dives on both Multiplayer and Zombies. Here’s what to expect prior to November 10:

[b]Blog 1: Pre-Season Preparation: [/b]A look back at Intel Drops, confirmation of Preload and Early Access Times, and confirmation of the rewards you receive for playing the Campaign. [url=https://www.callofduty.com/blog/2023/10/call-of-duty-modern-warfare-III-launch-comms-intel]Read more here[/url].

[b]Blog 2: Mapping Out Multiplayer: [/b]Details on the launch modes (3v3v3, 6v6, and 32v32), Additional Mode Intel, all the launch maps (both Core and Ground War), Carry Forward Maps, and the [i]Modern Warfare III[/i] Operators from SpecGru and Kortac. [url=https://www.callofduty.com/blog/2023/10/call-of-duty-modern-warfare-III-launch-comms-multiplayer-maps-modes-operators]Read more here[/url].

[b]Blog 3: Fully Equipped: A Deep Dive into Loadouts (MP, MWZ): [/b]You’re reading this Blog!

[b]Blog 4: Upping Your Arsenal: Primary and Secondary Weapons (MP, MWZ): [/b]All launch weapons are confirmed, including Aftermarket Parts, and a weapon-balancing pass. The Gunsmith receives a statistical overhaul, and we break this all down for you. [url=https://www.callofduty.com/blog/2023/11/call-of-duty-modern-warfare-III-launch-comms-weapons-detail]Read more here[/url].

[b]Blog 5: Cosmetic Customization: Weapon Camos (MP, MWZ): [/b]Could this be the biggest weapon progression feature in Call of Duty history? We detail the immense Multiplayer and Zombies Camo Challenge and Weapon Mastery system for your MWII and MWIII arsenal!

[b]Blog 6: Modern Warfare Zombies: Launch Content Overview: [/b]Join Operation Deadbolt, learning about the Mission structure, your Equipment and Zombies Field Upgrades, Acquisitions and Schematics, Acts, Tiers, Rewards and what to find during your deployments to the Exclusion Zone.

notes.title: Modern Warfare III Weapons Detail: What You Need to Know
notes.notes:
The Pre-season of Modern Warfare III brings an impressive arsenal of 37 different weapons to complement the 77 armaments carrying forward from Modern Warfare II and the six seasons of free weapon content. This brings the total number of weapons available to 114. Here’s some additional context to assist you as you build your weaponry from the largest selection ever seen in a Modern Warfare game:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/398f3d9cb566f67aaf9cf103f964a770e1a5ee05.jpg[/img]

[b]Primary Weapons: [/b]This is your main offensive weapon, and there is an impressive depth of choice, both in terms of weapon type and individual armaments within a particular category. Level up weapons to unlock attachments that can further increase a weapon’s capabilities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/25dfed7790a0f5edbc1a727885ce096518f72563.jpg[/img]

[b]Secondary Weapons: [/b]These are firearms or equipment that a player can carry in addition to their primary weapon. These secondary weapons serve various purposes and can be ued in different situations to complement the primary weapon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/49e75611af372200de9f0a3f621d557f962c3ccd.jpg[/img]

[b]Distinguishing Markers: [/b]Both [i]MWII[/i] and [i]MWIII[/i] weapons are easily distinguishable in the Weapon Select menus, as each features the logo of the game it originates from.

[b]Carry Forward Confirmation: [/b]If you’re a [i]Modern Warfare II[/i] player with a sizable collection of weapons, these are carried forward at the weapon level you reached, along with any unlocked attachments and camos. You can continue to unlock these weapons in [i]MWIII[/i].

[b]“Missing” [/b][b][i]MWII[/i][/b][b] Weapons: [/b]If you’re a brand-new [i]Modern Warfare[/i] player, or you’re a [i]MWII[/i] player who missed collecting some of the available weapons, every [i]MWII[/i] weapon is available in [i]MWIII[/i]. You simply complete an unlock Challenge in either Multiplayer, or extract the weapon if you find it during a [i]Modern Warfare Zombies[/i] session.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/9ba20d3c19c8e6d65e0b3c572ad0b9361c0a136c.jpg[/img]

[b]Weapons Balancing: [/b]All [i]MWII[/i] weapons will receive a weapons pass by Sledgehammer Games (see below) so that all armaments have balanced advantages (and shortfalls) no matter which [i]MW[/i] game they originated in.

[b]Weapon Selection Streamlining:[/b] There are shortcut buttons along the bottom of the screen allowing you to quickly Preview, Equip and Open Gunsmith, enter the Firing Range, or Preview the weapon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/8543de7a07c16448bf71a9c3dbaf961d20924b8d.jpg[/img]

[b]Attachments Available: [/b]Outside of the [i]MWII[/i] Riot Shield, all Primary Weapons and the Handgun Secondary Weapon category can be modified with attachments in Gunsmith.

[b]Assault Rifles (6 New)[/b]

[b]Total Available: [/b]15 ([i]MWII[/i]) + 6 ([i]MWIII[/i]) = 21.

Medium range Primary Weapons. Aiming down sights or Tac-Stance. Full-auto, usually. Average mobility. Often versatile due to attachment options.

[b]SVA 545[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/bd96b4416a92aa52c3331c17d12d0c646d5b841e.jpg[/img]

[i]This weapon system fires the first two rounds nearly at the same time, making this an incredibly lethal weapon in careful hands.[/i]

[b]MTZ-556[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/f03ea0a4a12970eae86a7b061e7c6d095c2fa0ec.jpg[/img]

[i]Boasting an exceptional fire rate for a 5.56 weapon, this close-quarters AR excels at close and mid-range.[/i]

[b]Holger 556[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/4b81c859aacb10c5ffceb90721f710d0236ed3d3.jpg[/img]

[i]Chambered in 5.56, this AR offers exceptional range and reliability for most engagements.[/i]

[b]MCW[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/9cc26b8bd794fcbfe45b8191a9394985cc2b7553.jpg[/img]

[i]This remarkably adaptable AR features phenomenal recoil control and versatility from a lightweight frame chambered in 5.56.[/i]

[b]DG-58[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/c1faf23f5e8589259d1f53d605f76fa94511cd5e.jpg[/img]

[i]With excellent recoil control and three-round burst fire, this bullpup AR dominates at mid- to long range.[/i]

[b]FR 5.56[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/ea59766c447398c32ee616385beef72dfa670169.jpg[/img]

[i]A three round burst bullpup AR. A well-placed burst can be extremely deadly at intermittent ranges.[/i]

[b]Battle Rifles (3 New)[/b]

[b]Total Available: [/b]5 ([i]MWII[/i]) + 3 ([i]MWIII[/i]) = 8.

Medium- to long-range Primary Weapons. Aiming down sights. Semi-auto or three-round burst, usually. Average mobility. High accuracy with high damage.

[b]BAS-B[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/93b1e1b1ae4764b5623c663f03e4f19f5d6a17b0.jpg[/img]

Secondary Weapons. Any range against technology or large groups. Aiming down sights. Single-load, usually. Low Mobility.

Fisticuffs range. Secondary Weapons aside from the Riot Shield, which is a Primary Weapon. Usually nonprojectile. Fastest mobility. Knives and other close-combat tools.

[b]Gutter Knife[/b]

[i]A small, curved talon-style blade. Extremely sharp and discreet for fast and deadly melee attacks.[/i]

[b]Aftermarket Parts (6 at Launch)[/b]

The following Aftermarket Parts are available immediately at launch, and each one has a designated unlock challenge. Expect further Aftermarket Parts to become available throughout each Season (including Pre-Season) via the Weekly Challenges system. To apply certain Aftermarket Parts to a weapon, the weapon needs to be at maximum level.

[b]Note: [/b]For Aftermarket Parts unlocked via Weekly Challenges, once the challenges expire at the end of the Season, the Aftermarket Part moves into the Armory Challenges section for a new (and always-available) unlock Challenge.

[b]JAK Raven Kit (MCW – AR)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/006badbb649f19f1ce0ec5968b4527f24b63d55e.jpg[/img]

Versatile and modular, this .300 conversion of the MCW can be adapted to hit hard in nearly every combat scenario. This Kit is unlockable in the first weekly challenge post-launch.

[b]JAK Heretic Carbine Kit (MTZ-762 – BR)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/bf3fdb7db66db558c7602fdd9aa7751c2a0180e2.jpg[/img]

This powerful, 7.62 AR was crafted to deliver exceptional damage with moderate recoil.

[b]Broodmother .45 Kit (WSP-9 – SMG)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/d3742c7f4825e74caf0e2cf1cf33ac96b66d6ec0.jpg[/img]

A high-damage conversion kit that rides the line between SMG and AR with hard-hitting .45 Auto rounds.

[b]JAK Annihilator Bullpup Kit (Pulemyot 762 – LMG)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/022282d1f707b56fb7d4a89d5bbbcf6c51355929.jpg[/img]

A modified, bullpup LMG that provides superior maneuverability while still delivering heavy and consistent fire.

[b]XRK IP-V2 Conversion Barrel (COR-45 – Handgun)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/eab7c5a4bccffffe5f1347faab34325d5c5f2a7b.jpg[/img]

This carbine conversion kit for the COR-45 allows for optics and underbarrel attachments. It also introduces binary fire which effectively doubles the fire rate.

[b]JAK Ferocity Carbine Kit (Renetti – Handgun)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/1ce335935b0119dad0fe9407dd4c50e12d90f325.jpg[/img]

This heavy carbine kit converts the Renetti pistol into a compact and maneuverable SMG. Allows for optics, stocks, and underbarrel attachments.

[b][i]Modern Warfare II[/i][/b][b] Weapon Balancing[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/661c00603ba19e1a40e1eea34dd96864ca28743b.jpg[/img]

The entire complement of the [i]Modern Warfare II[/i] weaponry will receive a weapon balancing pass by Sledgehammer Games, with additional adjustments after launch, as needed.

These aspects of [i]MWII[/i] weapons may be changed as part of this balancing pass:

Damage ranges

Damage values

Damage location multipliers (head, torso, legs)

Attachment value magnitudes (e.g., reducing [i]MWII[/i] laser ADS speeds)

Attachment PROS and CONS values

This weapon balancing pass will ensure weapons from MWII are optimized to perform alongside the new MWIII weapons arsenal, while maintaining the identity of the MWII weapons as much as possible.  The team will be observing weapons performance at launch and beyond as part of ongoing post-launch game refinements.

[b][i]Gunsmith: A Robust Weapon Builder (MP, MWZ)[/i][/b]

Expect the [i]Modern Warfare III[/i] Gunsmith to be an approachable, familiar, and vastly customizable weapon builder. Its goal is to make nearly every weapon in the game a true extension of your personal playstyle.

[b]Modifications and Attachments[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/70d57d394fafc9e3b6d003e8b1ba5ea731ca6772.jpg[/img]

As with [i]MWII[/i], building your weapon involves leveling up the weapon by obtaining Weapon XP (WXP) and unlocking modification slots to add attachments to your weapon. These attachments enhance your weapon’s performance. You can add up to five attachments to most weapons.

[b][i]MWIII[/i][/b][b] Aftermarket Parts: [/b]Some weapons have Aftermarket Parts, a modification system that dramatically after a weapon’s functionality and character. These unique upgrades are earned through weekly in-game challenges once a weapon reaches its max level. For even more information on Aftermarket Parts, [url=https://www.callofduty.com/blog/2023/10/call-of-duty-modern-warfare-III-gunsmith-innovations-aftermarket-parts]check out this blog[/url].

[b]Streamlined and Detailed: Gunsmith Statistics[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/4c341c43b86771db72cd75f479a6ccd2450e4f71.jpg[/img]

Based on community feedback, Sledgehammer Games has removed the Weapon Tuning feature present in MWII and has made further improvements to make Gunsmith easier to use. This change to Weapon Tuning applies to both MWII and MWIII weapons that utilize modifications.

[b]Statistical Refresher — Nine Important Stats: [/b]Within the Gunsmith are nine important and familiar values, which offer the same incredible detail and meticulous modification potential that [i]Call of Duty[/i] players are used to. Each aspect of an armament’s performance is related to the following statistics:

[b]          Damage: [/b]The points of damage you inflict on an enemy, dependent on where the area of the foe you hit, within the effective range of the weapon.

[b]Fire Rate: [/b]The rounds per minute and the rechamber time of the weapon.

[b]Range: [/b]The range that your weapon effectively inflicts the damage and the velocity of each bullet fired.

[b]Accuracy: [/b]The spread from hip fire in degrees, and how resistant to flinching while firing you are while employing the weapons.

[b]Recoil Control: [/b]The gun’s kick, as well as its horizontal and vertical recoil in degrees.

[b]Mobility: [/b]How quickly you can generally move, crouch and move, sprint, tactically sprint, and ADS while using the weapon.

[b]Handling: [/b]The ADS speed, reload quickness, sprint to fire speed, and weapon swap speed.

[b]Rounds:[/b] The number of individual pieces of ammunition (e.g., bullets or slugs) the weapon can fire before reloading is needed.

[b]Reserve:[/b] The additional ammunition the weapon carries. Once the Rounds and Reserve number is reduced to zero, you’re out of ammunition.

[b]PROS and CONS Values[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/a6e3542044cd744f8a27890347f42f65d6f0959f.jpg[/img]

Additional detail has been added to PROS and CONS of every weapon attachment. In [i]MWII[/i], this information was set out in a list format of (up to) four PROS and (up to) four CONS per attachment. In [i]MWIII[/i], each PRO and CON has an additional chevron icon to the left of each description, showcasing the following:

[b]          Single chevron:[/b] A minor PRO or CON.

[b]          Double chevron:[/b] A moderate PRO or CON.

[b]          Triple chevron:[/b] A strong PRO or CON.

[b]          Polygonal arrow:[/b] A new function of the mod.

This allows you to easily see how impressive (or disadvantageous) a particular PRO or CON of an attachment is as you build your chosen weapon in the Gunsmith.

[b]New Functions of Mods: [/b]Regarding the “polygonal arrow” that indicates a new modification function, this usually adds a new weapon function. Here are some examples of these that certain attachments bring to a weapon. These should be familiar to anyone who has played [i]MWII[/i]; they are just highlighted in a new manner. Here are a few examples:

[b]Muzzles:[/b] Undetectable by Radar (PRO), Flash Concealment (PRO).

[b]Ammunition: [/b]Bullet Penetration (PRO), Explosive Impact (PRO).

[b]Underbarrel: [/b]Bipod Mount (PRO).

[b]Lasers: [/b]Canted Laser Aiming (PRO), No Tactical Stance (CON).

[b]Optics: [/b]Different magnifications (PRO), Thermals (PRO), Sniper Glint (PRO).

[b]Modification Menu: Show Details[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/8b1c7aa31d49f8164c0e69c16057f9bad155f01b.jpg[/img]

Sledgehammer Games, in collaboration with Beenox, has added additional statistical depth for those players who need the finest incremental data for every aspect of every attachment. Select any of the modification menus around the weapon in the Gunsmith, and hit the Show Details button for an impressive, expanded view.

As you can see from the previous screen, this expanded view shows the seven statistical ratings of the weapon and breaks down how the attachment adds or subtracts from particular values. Cycle left and right and compare every attachment (of the same type) to determine how it affects weapon performance, down to a specific hit point, degree, millisecond, or increment of a meter!

[b]Weapon Stats: Filtering[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/eb3744490521eef109e924654a8941f07c764af3.jpg[/img]

Within a specific modification menu, or the Show Details submenu of a specific mod, is another option: Filtering. This allows you to fine-tune a weapon using only the statistics that are particularly important to you. You can:

            [b]Filter by statistic:[/b] This allows you to further compare attachments of the same type (i.e., an Optic, Barrel,  or Muzzle) with each other in regards to one, two, or up to seven of the main statistics. You can turn the filter off and on, allowing easy comparisons between mods , to further hone your own individual meta.

          [b]Filter by Attachement: [/b]You can also filter to show only attachments you’ve unlocked, or those you still need to unlock, so you know the granular information of an attachment before you fit it onto your armament. You can filter by Aftermarket Parts, too, as appropriate.

[b]Weapon Tuning Removal[/b]

With the additional statistical knowledge you’re able to receive while swapping between modifications, providing an impressive amount of incremental weapon meta building, Weapon Tuning has been removed, a feature that appeared in [i]Modern Warfare II[/i]. This change to Weapon Tuning applies to both MWII and MWIII weapons that utilize modifications.

[b][i]Modern Warfare III Launch Comms Continues[/i][/b]

Be sure to check back at the Call of Duty Blog between now and launch, as we confirm in-game content and offer deep dives on both Multiplayer and Zombies. Here’s what to expect prior to November 10:

[b]Blog 1: Pre-Season Preparation: [/b]A look back at Intel Drops, confirmation of Preload and Early Access Times, and confirmation of the rewards you receive for playing the Campaign. [url=https://www.callofduty.com/blog/2023/10/call-of-duty-modern-warfare-III-launch-comms-intel]Read it here.[/url]

[b]Blog 2: Mapping Out Multiplayer: [/b]Details on the launch modes (3v3v3, 6v6, and 32v32), Additional Mode Intel, all the launch maps (both Core and Ground War), Carry Forward Maps, and the [i]Modern Warfare III[/i] Operators from SpecGru and Kortac. [url=https://www.callofduty.com/blog/2023/10/call-of-duty-modern-warfare-III-launch-comms-multiplayer-maps-modes-operators]Read it here.[/url]

[b]Blog 3: Fully Equipped: A Deep Dive into Loadouts (MP, MWZ): [/b]Gear up for the evolution of Perks, with detailed confirmation on all the launch Equipment, including Vests, Gloves, Boots, and Gear. Tacticals, Lethals, Field Upgrades, and Killstreaks are also confirmed.

[b]Blog 4: Upping Your Arsenal: Primary and Secondary Weapons (MP, MWZ): [/b]You’re reading this Blog!

[b]Blog 5: Cosmetic Customization: Weapon Camos (MP, MWZ): [/b]Could this be the biggest weapon progression feature in Call of Duty history? We detail the immense Multiplayer and Zombies Camo Challenge and Weapon Mastery system for your MWII and MWIII arsenal! Coming soon.

[b]Blog 6: Modern Warfare Zombies: Launch Content Overview: [/b]Join Operation Deadbolt, learning about the Mission structure, your Equipment and Zombies Field Upgrades, Acquisitions and Schematics, Acts, Tiers, Rewards and what to find during your deployments to the Exclusion Zone. Coming soon.

Stay Frosty.

[i]

notes.title: Modern Warfare III Campaign Early Access is live now!
notes.notes:

Play the Campaign up to a week early* by pre-purchasing any digital edition of Modern Warfare III. 

Jump in to play the new action-packed story and dive into some of the new Open Combat Missions, in addition to the signature, cinematic Call of Duty campaign missions. Earn rewards for Modern Warfare III multiplayer by completing the Campaign, including new Calling Cards, Operators, Double XP Tokens, and more!

*Actual play time subject to possible outages and applicable time zone differences.

notes.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III Campaign: How to Play
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/178cd2ae5e1c33b359ad1282ed55fbc83f40a8d7.png[/img]


[olist]	[*][b]A direct sequel:[/b] [u]Modern Warfare III [/u]picks up immediately after the events of [u]Modern Warfare II[/u]. Join Captain Price and Task Force 141 as they face off against the ultimate threat, ultranationalist Vladimir Makarov.[/*]	[*][b]Open Combat Missions:[/b] New Open Combat Missions redefine the traditional Campaign level. Deploy to wide-open locations and gear up with Supply Boxes, Armor Plates, Vests, and more. Take a stealthy approach or grab a vehicle and drive head-on into danger.[/*]	[*][b]Mission completion rewards:[/b] Earn over a dozen in-game rewards for completing the Campaign, including new Calling Cards, Operators, Double XP Tokens, and a special Multiplayer Weapon Blueprint unlocked at game launch for Campaign completion.[/*][/olist]

From COD HQ, head to the [u]Modern Warfare III[/u] section and select the Campaign tile. Even though the game has already launched, we don’t want to spoil anything about it. Follow the prompts when starting the Campaign to choose your difficulty setting and then get right to it. The game will tell you everything you need to know to get started. Prepare for a wild ride.

[b]Choose Your Difficulty Level[/b]

The [u]Modern Warfare III[/u] Campaign features four difficulty levels. The higher the difficulty level, the greater the challenge. Note that you can change the game’s difficulty level at any time.

[b]Recruit: [/b]For players who are new to [u]Call of Duty[/u].

[b]Regular:[/b] Your abilities in combat will be tested.

[b]Hardened: [/b]Your skills will be strained.

[b]Veteran:[/b] You will not survive.

[b][u]Campaign Mission Rewards[/u][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/77fce7298aa3c5d0d2a61e86d182060e9af690eb.jpg[/img]

The Campaign consists of 14 different missions. All but one of these missions reward players with the following items upon completion:

[list]	[*][b]Operation 627:[/b] “Breather” Calling Card[/*]	[*][b]Precious Cargo:[/b] 30 mins Double Player XP Token & 30 mins Double Weapon XP Token[/*]	[*][b]Reactor:[/b] “Corso” Operator[/*]	[*][b]Payload: “[/b]Ghillie Guy” Calling Card[/*]	[*][b]Deep Cover:[/b] 30 mins XP Token and 30 mins Weapon XP Token[/*]	[*][b]Passenger:[/b] N/A[/*]	[*][b]Crash Site:[/b] “Pathfinder” Operator[/*]	[*][b]Flashpoint:[/b] “Toxic Drip” Calling Card[/*]	[*][b]Oligarch:[/b] 1 hour Double Player XP Token and 1 hour Double Weapon XP Token[/*]	[*][b]Highrise:[/b] “Doc” Operator[/*]	[*][b]Frozen Tundra:[/b] “Skull Rhapsody” Calling Card[/*]	[*][b]Gora Dam:[/b] 1 hour Double Player XP Token and 1 hour Double Weapon XP Token[/*]	[*][b]Danger Close:[/b] “Jabber” Operator[/*]	[*][b]Trojan Horse:[/b] Campaign Completion Emblem and Weapon Blueprint[/*][/list]

[h2][u]Open Combat Missions[/u][/h2]
[u]Modern Warfare III[/u] introduces Open Combat Missions (OCMs), which occur throughout the Campaign alongside more traditional single-player missions. OCMs redefine player agency, offering an unparalleled degree of freedom and greatly expanding the playable area.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/714c5d0ad836f77f2500d35c904f6695477bc20e.png[/img]

[olist]	[*][b]Fixed objective, endless possibilities:[/b] You’re there to complete the mission, but how you do it is up to you. Slip through like a shadow or go in loud and start blasting. Scavenge extra gear throughout the AO to suit your preferred playstyle.[/*]	[*][b]Seek out essential gear:[/b] While seeking out new weapons, Armor Plates, and other items, keep your eyes peeled for Ziplines and Ascenders. Often near objective locations, these items skyrocket your movement potential across the map.[/*]	[*][b]But they were just here: [/b]Caught off guard and outnumbered? Retreat into the environment, using your Ascender and Parachute to quickly get out of view. If the enemy loses sight of you for long enough, they will eventually stop their direct pursuit, and resort to searching the vicinity for you.[/*][/olist]

[b]Your Operator[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/514c18e6b2857ad2d40efb2a869a965e0f663055.jpg[/img]

Open Combat Missions require the best of the best. In each mission, you will deploy as a designated member of Task Force 141: Farah, Ghost, Gaz, Soap, or Price.

In your first playthrough of an OCM, your Operator is assigned a starting Loadout according to the mission’s narrative, including the Spotter Scope to better scan the environment for enemy threats, tagging enemies, locating equipment, and discovering information about points of interest. One of your first tasks is to seek out better gear, of which there is an abundance, found throughout the area of operations.

[b]Gear Up[/b]

Expect to find all sorts of useful items in OCMs, including new weapons, Equipment, Field Upgrades, and even Armaments (that Multiplayer Operators know as “Killstreaks”) that will boost your offensive and defensive capabilities. Of particular importance, however, are the Parachute, Ascender, and Armor Plate Carrier upgrades.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/2800a6efe49669de5b8f726949c1e7bfeb6fe574.jpg[/img]

[b]Parachute:[/b] The Parachute is a game changer, allowing you to safely jump from great heights and soar over long distances. Follow the button prompt when jumping from a high point to activate the Parachute. When you’re close to landing, your Operator will automatically cut the rope and return to a standing position, or you can cut the cord manually to force a landing.

[b]Ascender:[/b] Going up! The Ascender helps you reach the highest points on the map. With this item, you can zip up ropes that lead to places in key positions throughout the environment, or ziplines to move across long horizontal distances. Use your elevated or newly-acquired position to escape a problematic situation, snipe from a distance, or, if you’ve got the Parachute, reposition far from your current location.

[b]Plate Carrier Upgrade Vest: [/b]Initially, your Operator can only equip one Armor Plate at a time, a reasonable-enough defense in minor battles but lacking when the action gets hectic. Find a Plate Carrier Upgrade Vest to increase the number of Armor Plates you can equip at a time. When you first find the Vest, your carrying capacity will increase to two Armor Plates, and then three after finding another one. Now you’re ready for anything.

[b]Getting Around: Your Tac Map and Minimap[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/28204aa4b74705753a9b533d461d0550e046447a.jpg[/img]

[b]Tac Map[/b]

The Tac Map is of essential importance, providing an overview of the objective and its location. A legend indicates the position of important items, and a tracker shows your most important gear and the weapons and items you’ve discovered in the level.

When first deploying into an OCM, the majority of the Tac Map will be covered in a fog of war. As you explore the environment, the fog will be lifted, revealing greater environmental detail.

[b]Minimap[/b]

Use the minimap to pinpoint items in your immediate surroundings without needing to pull up your Tac Map. Discovered weapons, Supply Boxes, Field Upgrades, and other Armaments will be displayed here along with the objective location and other points of interest.

[b]Enemy Alert Levels: [/b]The minimap is also your cue to the enemy’s current alert level. When you’ve been seen, the borders will turn yellow, indicating that they are aware of something in the vicinity without knowing your exact location. If found — or if you initiate the attack — the borders will turn red to show that they know where you are. At this time, an enemy may even throw the alarm to call in reinforcements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/198f7805c2a977457e2bd25e2a66374f186d4ba3.jpg[/img]

The enemies themselves also follow this color-coded system. Red dots on the minimap indicate enemies rushing to engage in combat, while yellow dots represent enemies on the lookout.

With fast movement and clever repositioning, it’s possible to get out of the alert state. Red will revert to yellow when they’ve lost you but are still on guard for your whereabouts, and then will return to a less aggressive state  if you continue to remain out of sight. At this point, you can resume your stealth operations, or just get into a better position before going guns blazing again.

[b]Play It Again[/b]

OCMs reward exploration and repeated playthroughs with weapons and items found throughout the level. When you replay an OCM, you get to customize your starting Loadout based on the weapons and items you’ve found in previous playthroughs.

Start the mission with your Parachute and Ascender already in hand, plus any extra Armor Plate carrying capacity earned through Vests. Use your enhanced starting gear to push into higher difficulty levels and/or try out new tactics.

[b][u]Top 5 Tips for Open Combat Missions[/u][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/338f0786baf1363bc8d92008d45eb65276e2a3c1.jpg[/img]

[b]1. There’s always another way.[/b] Grab a vehicle and race past the sentries straight to the objective; dive into the water and reposition out of sight; use your Parachute to soar over enemy encampments. OCMs offer endless possibilities in how you approach the task at hand. If something’s not working, revisit your tactics and take a new approach.

[b]2. The right gear for the job.[/b] While at first, you’ll need to make do with the gear you’re provided, with enough exploration and scavenging, you’ll soon a wider variety of equipment that can best suit your style of play. If you’re going stealth, Throwing Knives and a Recon Drone are better choices than Frag Grenades and unsuppressed weapons and vice versa.

[b]3. Know your enemy. [/b]Even if you’re not going the stealth route, it pays to stay out of sight and scout nearby enemy positions. Look for red vehicles on the minimap indicating enemy patrols, and scan the horizon for snipers and other threats you might miss when rushing straight in. Regardless of your approach, that intel will help you make better decisions in the heat of the moment.

[b]4. Build up your arsenal.[/b] OCMs encourage replayability through the accumulation of weapons and items found in the level. Use your arsenal to build out the perfect Loadout on subsequent playthroughs and get right to the task at hand without first needing to scavenge for the proper supplies.

[b]5. Ramp up the challenge.[/b] Use your expanded arsenal on subsequent playthroughs to push into higher difficulty levels. Tackling an OCM on Veteran is much more manageable when deploying with your preferred Loadout.

Stay frosty.

[i]© 2023 Activision Publishing, Inc. ACTIVISION, CALL OF DUTY, and MODERN WARFARE are trademarks of Activision Publishing, Inc. All other trademarks and trade names are the property of their respective owners.

For more information, please visit www.callofduty.com and www.youtube.com/callofduty, and follow @Activision and @CallofDuty on X, Instagram, and Facebook. For Call of Duty Updates, follow @CODUpdates on X.[/i]

notes.title: Multiplayer Maps and Modes: What You Need to Know
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/48cfacf08e86f99845716906daa57e8f58ea123a.jpg[/img]

Expect the following launch modes scheduled for rotation in the available Playlists, with more Standard and Alternate Modes being added in the following weeks.

[b]3v3v3 Mode[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/02a5571538e5ae1bd1fb4036c257e71d8226e3b1.jpg[/img]

[b]Cutthroat: [/b][u]Three teams go head to head[/u] . . . [u]to head. First team to reach the round win limit wins.[/u]

[b]6v6 Modes[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/7ced695190a1b027d46cbfa4ec14acb6bb47a6d6.jpg[/img]

[b]Team Deathmatch: [/b][u]An exercise in attrition. Eliminate enemy players until the score limit is reached to win.[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/34297aac81855b2afa46b9ccbceaf21b6b669ee6.jpg[/img]

[b]Domination: [/b][u]Capture, hold and defend objectives to earn points. First team to the score limit wins.[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/9b6c8e55db40609b020aeed1740ffe3e33f45fa5.jpg[/img]

[b]Search & Destroy: [/b][u]Teams alternate between detonating and defusing a bomb. No respawns.[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/1fcfccaf43d018374fe6d2a9875293cdce42cb90.jpg[/img]

[b]Kill Confirmed: [/b][u]Recover dog tags to score for your team and deny enemy scores.[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/de4a592b34409f870aa6009dbd4ec5af2a91c185.jpg[/img]

[b]Free-For-All: [/b][u]Defeat everyone. The first player to reach the score limit ends the game. The top three players win.[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/92a4de07c8e301e0d8647b892b8308e64ef6cb60.jpg[/img]

[b]Hardpoint: [/b][u]Capture the Hardpoint and hold it against attack. The first team to reach the score limit wins.[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/d792643d90c0a01813eb72708cef56e74bbe7545.jpg[/img]

[b]Control: [/b][u]Take turns attacking and defending the objective.[/u]

[b]War: [/b][u]Progress through linear objectives to push the battle line and win.[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/50ae2d689f303b887aa351c4d89bdc640a39d44d.jpg[/img]

[b]Gun Game: [/b][u]Be the first player to score a kill with each one of the provided weapons.[/u]

[b]32v32 Modes[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/790503f14eae06906dcfa7c34d97da6136b8b936.jpg[/img]

[b]Ground War: [/b][u]Large-scale conflict featuring vehicles. Capture and hold objectives to score. Captured objectives open forward spawning locations for your team.[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/c0992e49ee0288c67b9dc9e6a37f68d2c68340c1.jpg[/img]

[b]Invasion: [/b][u]A massive and chaotic battle with a mix of Players and AI fighting alongside each other and against each team.[/u]

[b]Additional Mode Intel[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/f31b403c2599ec19e5c73b79702baec6a712dc05.jpg[/img]

[b]Hardcore:[/b] Features a limited HUD, low health, friendly fire enabled, and other changes to gameplay; this is also scheduled for launch.

[b]The Firing Range: [/b]This returns with the familiar three-dummy corridor to practice in. Bring in any Loadout, swapping weapons, modifications, and your Perks (Vest, Gloves, Boots and Gear) while you practice. The usual shelving and bars allow you to mount and fire at different heights.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/ba547d1d52ac2377d70674a511ec91020630edd8.jpg[/img]

[b]Private Matches (Training and Benchmark): [/b]As ever, Private Matches are a great way to look through (and tweak) all the game settings for every type of mode, and they allow you to explore the available maps. In addition, expect a [b]Training Course[/b] where you can learn basic movements and combat skills as you navigate one of the launch Core 6v6 maps as a solo player.

[b][u]Play: Launch Maps (Multiplayer)[/u][/b]

An impressive number of modernized [u]Modern Warfare 2[/u] (2009) maps are part of the initial map pool, along with three Ground War maps (based on points of interest within the Urzikstan Big Map) and a linear section of the massive Urzikstan itself (War mode).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/7a309916d8d1ecc8daef6e699d55d18627f25bc2.jpg[/img]

[b]Afghan (Core): [/b]Battle in the arid desert canyons around a crash site, encircled by bunkers and cliffside anti-air batteries poised to take down incoming aircraft. The uneven terrain presents risk and opportunity, from the high cliff face above to the dark cave below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/406b8cfd3fc32479a5f69733193e29aa9693f40b.jpg[/img]

[b]Derail (Core): [/b]Snow blankets the forest surrounding a railway town and its facilities. At the center, a trainwreck has scattered railcars over the landscape. Take the lead on this large map and leave your enemies out cold in the woods.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/ebb51e2334899585877480cb549bb89840f1cbf8.jpg[/img]

[b]Estate (Core): [/b]Head to a secluded getaway in the Caucasus Mountains, where a pristine lodge overlooks an expansive woodland property. Fight from the main living quarters or utilize the various outbuildings and fields to engage enemies from the perimeter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/57ff9ea074876bff97c2bc325664489388e16be4.jpg[/img]

[b]Favela (Core): [/b]Drop into the slums of Rio de Janeiro as bystanders scramble to escape the scene of the oncoming skirmish. Brave the tightly clustered center, fire down on enemies from the rooftops, or stick to the perimeter and eliminate enemies from afar.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/d654cc2e4f8bf127d0d76f5dae4cf10cf54d38ff.jpg[/img]

[b]Highrise (Core): [/b]Whatever you do, don’t look down. This midsized map consists of two opposite facing buildings over a central rooftop worksite. Tunnels wind below the surface and an imposing Helipad offers access to some of the map’s best vantage points alongside other perilous crossings for the brave and foolhardy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/8d67728cba94e2a2e5b267828f8fa3fba499f5fa.jpg[/img]

[b]Invasion (Core): [/b]Deploy to a battle-torn, medium-sized Multiplayer map featuring tightknit buildings, close street fighting, and long-distance vantage points. In this urban layout, Operators must act fast and smart, turning the map’s risks into advantages.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/35384f3e7feed29022f83ab60fd22cd3681a1f85.jpg[/img]

[b]Karachi (Core): [/b]Keep your eyes sharp and your head on a swivel; this map challenges Operators with a compact urban setting packed with climbing opportunities and routes for every playstyle. A keen understanding of the layout will help you prepare for your next drop into this medium-sized Multiplayer map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/8d3ec73e9f4bc33802e769f50c8efeb7ff9fe548.jpg[/img]

[b]Quarry (Core): [/b]This open-pit mine in a wide-open map features plenty of long-distance fights down the center Crane and side lanes. Quarry is punctuated by close-range battles in the offices and warehouses. Climbing opportunities abound. Or bring the fight indoors where multilevel buildings provide room to move and windows that overlook huge swaths of the map. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/ef9f521a906d23c602b1b521a42ab09a01d11280.jpg[/img]

[b]Rundown (Core): [/b]Infiltrate a South American village where a low-running river divides the main settlement from its more sparsely populated Outback. Group your forces when attempting to make a crossing and watch those corners when weaving through the cluster of buildings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/80997e283721212700a552ccb4436b8756e56d00.jpg[/img]

[b]Rust (Core): [/b]Located in the oil fields of the Urzikstan desert, Rust is a small, square map dominated by its central tower. Fight for your spot up top or use the map’s various obstacles to stay out of sight while you skirmish on the ground. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/30a065f52023dcb675b74b9631decf614565be54.jpg[/img]

[b]Scrapyard (Core): [/b]Battle in an aircraft boneyard surrounded by buildings overlooking the wreckage within. Flank enemies by racing through the fuselages and watch your head when sniper battles erupt between the two main warehouses.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/7d6057313115584ef7e613f9ad4760471820e8bf.jpg[/img]

[b]Skidrow (Core): [/b]Deploy to a midsized urban landscape dominated by the central block. Smaller buildings around the perimeter provide further vantage points, and the streets throughout give savvy Operators the means to flank and outmaneuver their enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/9800379895b1a44b48d2243568fc9db4cc9589a1.jpg[/img]

[b]Sub Base (Core): [/b]Submarines dock for maintenance and refueling at a naval base on the high seas. Deploy dockside and battle for control over the locale — a midsized map packed with vantage points, flanking routes, and a deadly center ground where only the most stalwart Operators dare pass.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/e89dab9dea61a8f4f9a83cf1e4bd27be8bc3cc10.jpg[/img]

[b]Terminal (Core): [/b]Infiltrate an International Airport and battle across one of the most infamous locales of all. Try your luck inside the terminal or take the fight to the Apron. All playstyles have their place on this midsized, classic Multiplayer map, so gear up how you want and get ready for departure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/535ec23a59c3dd7fb6e9231d233c80fd6dabfadb.jpg[/img]

[b]Underpass (Core): [/b]Pouring rain has transformed this run-down South American industrial sector into a mud bath, but that won’t stop Operator skirmishes. Tromp through the mud, stage an ambush, or test your luck on the rain-slicked rooftops. In this large environment, your climbing and ambush options are nearly endless.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/103a49f4b8eb7a2c334def05bb00da4b871e20a1.jpg[/img]

[b]Wasteland (Core): [/b]Battle across an abandoned Wasteland, where wide-open fields encourage sniper battles all around. If extreme close range is more your speed, try your luck in the Dugout, a tight underground crossroads where all trenches meet in the middle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/9e346b675c048d1fdac010206397c587308a99ad.jpg[/img]

[b]Levin Resort (Ground War): [/b]Tourists and business travelers alike used to flock to the Levin Resort, enjoying the poolside seating and abundant shopping and services within. It’s now a vacant site, the nearby statues of General Barkov defaced following his downfall. Tread carefully through the resort courtyard, where vantage points from multiple angles present danger to those below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/4372ff4d369ce7bae141694a84ad55aad54d329c.jpg[/img]

[b]Orlov Military Base (Ground War): [/b]Missile silos lie at the heart of the Orlov Military Base alongside bunkers and facilities built into the mountainous terrain that dominates the northern portion of the map. Scattered barricades throughout provide squads with a means of defense when pushing into the area.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/33612ee198e787569e607ac84ebe4aaadb1bf61f.jpg[/img]

[b]Popov Power (Ground War): [/b]The workhorse of Urzikstan, Popov Power supplies energy to the growing region. Fight around the plant’s cooling towers and containment structures and utilize the full run of its industrial buildings to flank and ambush enemy squads.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/a1af50d7c9e2b5b04615ac7416a766d2cefe2b82.jpg[/img]

[b]Operation: Spearhead (War Mode): [/b]At launch, the first location within Operation Spearhead is the large-scale Urzikstan map, inside a linear corridor within the Orlov Military Base and Kadurin Silo. Clear anti-aircraft defenses so armored vehicles can be airdropped, staying close to the armor to break through to the launch site and set up missile overrides in this thrilling 6v6 battle!

[b][u]Modern Warfare II[/u][/b][b]: Carry Forward Maps[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/b31871315bcb1e56eb93fbc641af6ff08a12e4ca.jpg[/img]

To further augment an already-impressive selection of Core 6v6 maps, we are excited to announce that a number of fan-favorite [u]Modern Warfare II[/u] maps will gradually become available to play in [u]Modern Warfare III[/u] throughout the live seasons. The initial selection — scheduled to be four Core 6v6 maps that include Farm 18, Mercado, and Shoot House — will become available shortly after launch in a dedicated Playlist, and more will follow throughout the Live Seasons. Here's some beneficial intel about these additions:

These maps are graphically identical to how they appeared in [u]MWII[/u], and due to the innovations to movement and general gameplay mechanics present in [u]MWIII[/u], you may find that they play in an altogether different manner.

These maps are completely additive, meaning they are scheduled to appear [u]in addition to[/u] a full complement of new (and remastered) seasonal maps and other content.

New [u]MWIII[/u] modes (such as Cutthroat) will not be playable on these Carry Forward [u]MWII[/u] maps.

[b][u]Operators: SpecGru and KorTac Reinforcements[/u][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/40635dc84b50ba2fa96cdca65fc08028d9717cc2.jpg[/img]

Expect 25 additional [u]Modern Warfare III [/u]Operators (13 SpecGru, 12 KorTac) to bolster the Operator pool, allowing you to select from a total of over 90 different Operators across [u]MWII[/u] and [u]MWIII[/u]. Some Operators are instantly accessible. Locked Operators can be unlocked via in-game challenges or purchased in-Store. Any [u]MWII[/u] Operators you have acquired will be carried forward and can be used in [u]MWIII[/u]. [url=https://www.callofduty.com/blog/2023/08/call-of-duty-modern-warfare-II-to-modern-warfare-III-carry-forward]Read more about Carry Forward here[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501705/2f9be7d7bf62fc678f3dd5a5a4289222b48bc8ba.jpg[/img]

[b]SpecGru Operators (13):[/b]

[b]Price: [/b]Nemesis Reactive Skin available via [u]MWIII[/u] Vault Edition purchase.

[b]Ghost: [/b]Nemesis Reactive Skin available via [u]MWIII[/u] Vault Edition purchase.

[b]Blueprint (Mil-Sim): [/b]Initially available.

[b]Rocket (Mil-Sim): [/b]Initially available.

[b]Byline: [/b]Unlocked after completing a challenge in Multiplayer.

[b]Scorch: [/b]Unlocked after completing a challenge in Modern Warfare Zombies.

[b]Ripper: [/b]Unlocked after completing a challenge in Modern Warfare Zombies.

[b]Pathfinder: [/b]Unlocked after completing a Campaign Challenge.

[b]Warrior: [/b]Available after purchasing the Call of Duty Endowment “Warrior” Pack, available November 10.

[b]Riptide: [/b]Unlocked after completing a challenge in Multiplayer.

[b]BBQ: [/b]Unlocked after completing a challenge in Multiplayer.

[b]Jabber: [/b]Unlocked after completing a Campaign Challenge.

[b]Jet: [/b]Unlocked after completing a challenge in Multiplayer.

[b]KorTac Operators (11):[/b]

[b]          Warden: [/b]Operator and Nemesis Reactive Skin available via [u]MWIII[/u] Vault Edition purchase.

[b]          Makarov: [/b]Operator and Nemesis Reactive Skin available via [u]MWIII[/u] Vault Edition purchase.

[b]Blaze (Mil-Sim): [/b]Initially available.

[b]Thirst (Mil-Sim): [/b]Initially available.

[b]Alpine: [/b]Unlocked after completing a challenge in Multiplayer.

[b]          Enigma: [/b]Unlocked after completing a challenge in Multiplayer.

[b]Bantam: [/b]Unlocked after completing a challenge in Multiplayer.

[b]          Doc: [/b]Unlocked after completing a Campaign Challenge.

[b]          Raptor: [/b]Unlocked after completing a challenge in Multiplayer.

[b]Corso: [/b]Unlocked after completing a Campaign Challenge.

[b]Swagger: [/b]Unlocked after completing a challenge in Multiplayer.

[b]Operator Customization: [/b]Select the Operator (whether from [u]MWII[/u] or [u]MWIII[/u]) from the main menu to check out their Customization Options, like additional Skins, Finishing Moves and biographical information.

[b][u]Modern Warfare III Launch Comms Continues[/u][/b]

Be sure to check back at the Call of Duty Blog between now and launch, as we confirm in-game content and offer deep dives on both Multiplayer and Zombies. Here’s what to expect prior to November 10:

[b]Blog 1: Pre-Season Preparation: [/b]A look back at Intel Drops, confirmation of Preload and Early Access Times, and confirmation of the rewards you receive for playing the Campaign.

[b]Blog 2: Mapping Out Multiplayer: [/b]You’re reading this Blog!

[b]Blog 3: Fully Equipped: A Deep Dive into Loadouts (MP, MWZ): [/b]Gear up for the evolution of Perks, with detailed confirmation on all the launch Equipment, including Vests, Gloves, Boot, and Gear. Tacticals, Lethals, Field Upgrades, and Killstreaks are also confirmed.

[b]Blog 4: Upping Your Arsenal: Primary and Secondary Weapons (MP, MWZ): [/b]All launch weapons are confirmed, including Aftermarket Parts, and a weapon-balancing pass. The Gunsmith receives a statistical overhaul, and we break this all down for you.

[b]Blog 5: Cosmetic Customization: Weapon Camos (MP, MWZ): [/b]Could this be the biggest weapon progression feature in Call of Duty history? We detail the immense Multiplayer and Zombies Camo Challenge and Weapon Mastery system for your MWII and MWIII arsenal!

[b]Blog 6: Modern Warfare Zombies: Launch Content Overview: [/b]Join Operation Deadbolt, learning about the Mission structure, your Equipment and Zombies Field Upgrades, Acquisitions and Schematics, Acts, Tiers, Rewards and what to find during your deployments to the Exclusion Zone.
